title: Actual costs
content:
### Actual costs
In the same way as for planned costs there are actual costs for activities, manufacturing, and other. For activities and manufacturing, the actual time spent and reporting (post-calculation) are shown. The planned costs' total is suggested for other costs. However, you can add, delete, and change this.
The total time and cost are shown as a total at the bottom of the box.

title: Correction (existing manufacturing order)
content:
### Correction (existing manufacturing order)
Here you can link one or several operations to the case if you are to correct a problem on an existing manufacturing order.
By clicking the Add new row at the end (F5) button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_add_row.png), a dialog opens where you can enter a manufacturing order number and then you see the order structure including operations. Once you have selected operations in the dialog you will here see them as rows. For each row you can select if material cost, subcontracting cost, and processing cost, should be charged on the operation. If none of the CM The contribution margin (CM) is the difference between the standard price and the sales price., CS, and CP checkboxes are marked on the row, nothing will be charged for the correction.

title: Basic information
content:
### Basic information
In this box you fill in basic information for the case type.

#### Status
Here you select the status of the case. Automatic status changes are always updated upwards. The status of a case is, e.g., never changed back to Printed if it already has a higher status. The different status steps are:
1 – Registered
2 – Printed
3 – Started
4 – Closed
9 – Historical
99 – Rejected.

#### Case category
By clicking the Category selection button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_more_info.png), you can select a category if categories have been registered in the Categories procedure. If no categories are registered, you can type as you please in this field. Categories can be used as a selection term in different lists. Read more about how categories can be created/constructed in the online help function for the [Categories](../../../GeneralRegisters/Categories/Categories/wCategories.htm) procedure.

#### Customer's/Supplier's Reference
You can select the person who is the reference for the customer or supplier on the case.

#### Customer's/Supplier's case number
It is possible to enter the customer's or the supplier's case number for the following case types: Customer nonconformity and Supplier nonconformity. For the customer's case number you can enter 40 characters. For the supplier's case number you can enter 20 characters.

#### Our Reference
Here you can select the person to be your own reference for the case.

#### Case date
Here you enter the date that will be the registration date or start date of the case. You can enter a date which is either earlier or later than the date when the case is created.

#### Finish date
Here you enter the date that will be the finish date of the case.
Initial delivery
Under the Initial delivery button, you enter the information that applies to the initial delivery to which the nonconformity part belongs. The fields are filled in automatically if there is data available. The fields are available for the case types customer nonconformity and supplier nonconformity.

#### Order number
Here you enter the order number of the initial delivery to which the part belongs. The number you enter is validated against the customer/supplier.

#### Arrival reported/Delivery quantity
Here you enter the quantity the initial arrival/delivery consisted of.

#### Delivery date
Enter the date when the initial delivery was made.

#### Project
Here you enter the project to which the initial delivery belongs.

#### Invoice/consecutive number
Here you enter the invoice number that was used when the delivery was invoiced, alternatively, you enter the consecutive number the invoice of the arrival was assigned.
Initial manufacturing
By clicking the Initial manufacturing button you can enter information about the initial purchase.

#### Manufacturing order
If the part is manufactured by you, you can link the manufacturing order information to the case. If the part is delivered to you, you can enter the manufacturing order of the initial manufacturing of the nonconformity part.

#### Operation
Here you can enter the operation number, if the nonconformity can be traced to a certain operation.

#### Work center
Here you can enter the work center, if the nonconformity can be traced to a certain operation.

#### Manufactured quantity
Here you can enter the manufactured quantity where the initial production of the claimed part took place. This is a numerical field with two decimals. If the part number has been entered you will see the part's standard unit in the field. By default, here is no value in the field. The field becomes automatically filled in with the finished quantity of manufacturing order if it is finished.

#### Manufacturing date
Here you can enter the finish date when the initial production of the claimed part took place. This is empty by default. If there is a finish date from the manufacturing order, this is filled in automatically.
Initial purchase
By clicking the Initial purchase button you can enter information about the initial purchase order.

#### Purchase order
If the part is purchased, you can link the purchase order to the case. If the order contains multiple part numbers, you select which part number/numbers the case concerns.

#### Arrival reported qty
The arrival reported quantity of the part which the claim concerns. Enter the quantity with two decimals. If the part number has been entered you will see the part's standard unit in the field. By default, here is no value in the field.

#### Delivery date
Here the delivery date for the initial arrival is shown.

title: Cause of nonconformity
content:
### Cause of nonconformity
Here you can choose a rejection code as the cause of the nonconformity in cases when the cause can be linked to such a code.
Here you can also choose a supplier as the cause of the nonconformity in cases when the nonconformity can be linked to a supplier. It can be e.g. a subcontract, a transport damage, or a delivery of incorrect material.
Enter the material's part number if the cause origins from a faulty incorporated material in a manufactured part.
For customer nonconformity or internal nonconformity you can enter a work center or department if the cause can be tied to any of these parties.
You can also enter a cause description and link files.

title: Comment/Files
content:
### Comment/Files
In this box you can add comments and link documents.

#### Customer/Supplier comment
Here you see comments entered for the customer in the customer register or comments entered for the supplier in the supplier register. The comment is not printed on any documents. The files you link here can only be displayed. They cannot be printed together with the case documents.

#### Internal comment
Here you can enter an internal comment regarding the case. It can be shown on the internal nonconformity report via settings for the document. The text is also visible e.g. in the Case list procedure. The files you link here cannot be printed automatically.

#### External comment
Here you can enter an external comment for the case. It can be shown on the case documents via case form settings. The text is also visible e.g. in the Case list procedure. The files you link here are possible to choose for automatic printout.

title: Comment/Files
content:
### Comment/Files

#### Comment
Here you enter/see comments regarding the costs. By clicking this button you access a text editor where you can write and format text, insert images and signature, and hyperlinks, etc. When a comment/text exists, the symbol on the button will change from an empty speech bubble ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_no_comment.png) to a filled speech bubble ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_comment.png).

#### Files
By clicking the Files button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_file_link.png), it is possible to link different files related to a comment or an instruction for the record in question. When the setting Automatic printout is available for activation, you can choose to get the linked file automatically printed. Read more in the topic [General features](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LinkFiles) about how to link files, automatic printout, and where linked files can be automatically printed. If there are linked files, you will see this symbol ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_file_linked.png) on the button.

title: Communication
content:
### Communication
In this box you register communication information for the case. This includes phone numbers, mobile phone numbers, fax numbers, and e-mail addresses. For e-mail address you can determine if the address should be recipient of different documents according to the following. If the customer/supplier does not have a Recipient of entered in the Customer register or Supplier register respectively, the reference entered in the case will be used instead.
Add communication addresses from template ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_add_template.png) – adds communication addresses from a template that has been created in the Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Case procedure. These templates can contain both internal and external addresses.
For customer nonconformities:
The e-mail address can be recipient the documents Confirmation and Response.
For supplier nonconformities:
The e-mail address can be recipient the document Claim report.
For internal nonconformities and own nonconformity types:
The e-mail address can be recipient the document Nonconformity report.

title: Confirmed rejection
content:
### Confirmed rejection
Not used for 8D.
If you, during the handling of the case, realize that the rejection code or the number of rejections initially entered were not correct, you can change the information in this box. It might for example be a customer who has provided you with information about a certain error or a certain number of rejections. At a later stage, it might be discovered that the error depends on another reason or that the number of rejections was not correct. You can then enter the new information in this box and it will override the information provided initially.
If the rejection code and the number of rejections was correctly stated at the start, this box does not need to be used to verify it.

title: Credit invoice
content:
### Credit invoice
If the customer should be credited or if the supplier will send you a credit invoice, you use this box.

#### Customer nonconformity
If the customer should be credited for the costs that the rejected parts have caused, this is handled in this box. You can link an existing credit invoice by entering the order number.
Using the More info button you will see the order header. There you can see information about the customer and the delivery address.
By using the preview ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_form_viewing.png), you can print or send the invoice by e-mail. A link between the case and the credit invoice is created when saving.

#### Supplier nonconformity
If the supplier is to send you a credit invoice for the rejected parts, you check Request credit. After this you enter the consecutive number the supplier credit invoice got at the registration. A validation will be made in order to check that the invoice is of type credit and belongs to the supplier registered on the case. The consecutive number is filled in automatically, if the invoice is linked to the arrival. If the order has been created separately, you can enter the consecutive number manually.

title: D0 Background
content:
### D0 Background
Here you enter necessary background information regarding the case.

#### Case date
Here you enter the date when the case was created. Today's date is entered by default in this field, but it can be changed.

#### Customer's reference
The person suggested in the Customer’s reference field is the person set as the default reference in the customer register. But it is possible to select among all references registered for the customer. If you start typing in the field, the system will suggest the reference that matches what you have typed.

#### Customer's case number
Here you can enter the customer's case number.

#### Our reference
Here you can select among the persons in the company who are registered as references in the personnel records. If you start typing in the field, the system will suggest the reference that matches what you have typed. The Our reference field will by default show the name linked to the logged-in user. If no such link exists, the user’s most recently selected Our reference, will be suggested.

#### Initial delivery
By clicking the button you can enter information about the initial delivery.

#### Initial manufacturing
By clicking the button you can enter information about the initial manufacturing order.

#### Initial purchase
By clicking the button you can enter information about the initial purchase.

title: D1 Establish a team
content:
### D1 Establish a team
Here you add the persons included in the team to solve this case.
Here you can add communication information for the persons included in the team to solve this case. You can modify, delete, and add rows containing communication information for the record in question.

title: D2 Describe the problem
content:
### D2 Describe the problem

#### Rejection code
Here you enter the rejection code provided by the customer in the claim. Rejection codes are handled in the Rejection codes/Error codes procedure.

#### No. of rejections
Here you enter the number of rejections that the case refers to.

#### Rejection description
In this field you can enter a rejection description and a translation of it. By clicking the button Insert phrase ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_add_phrase.png) it is possible to insert different phrases which are registered in the Phrases procedure.By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

#### Serial number
In this field you select the serial number for the product which the claim concerns, if the customer/supplier can specify it. A validation will be made against the customer/supplier and you will get a warning if the serial number is not linked.

#### Batch number
In this field you select/see the batch number to which the nonconforming part belonged at arrival reporting. It is also possible to enter a batch number that is not registered. This field is only available for the case type Supplier nonconformity.

#### Part
Here you can enter the part number of the product which the claim concerns. You can either enter it or it is automatically filled in if you enter the serial number. If the part has an active revision, this is automatically filled in in the field below. However, it is possible to edit the revision if the claim refers to a previous revision.

#### Name
Here you see the part name.

#### Revision
Here you can enter the part's revision which the cases concerns. The revision is set to the part's active revision when the part number is entered.

#### Internal comment
Here you can enter an internal comment regarding the case. It can be shown on the internal nonconformity report via settings for the document. The text is also visible e.g. in the Case list procedure. The files you link here cannot be printed automatically.

#### External comment
Here you can enter an external comment for the case. It can be shown on the case documents via case form settings. The text is also visible e.g. in the Case list procedure. The files you link here are possible to choose for automatic printout.

title: D3-D8 Activities
content:
### D3-D8 Activities
Here you add the activities required to be performed to solve the case. You can insert activity templates from the procedure Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Case.

title: Default Part
content:
### Default Part

#### Cause code
Here you enter the cause code provided by the customer in the claim. Rejection codes are handled in the Rejection codes/Error codes procedure.

#### Number of rejections
Enter the number of rejections that the case refers to. When the case is saved with a number of rejections and part number entered, you can, by using the info meny or the button to the right of the field, go to the field go to the Direct stock reporting procedure and have the part number and quantity filled in for withdrawal. The link is only available if the system setting Affect balance for case is set to Yes and you have saved the case.

#### Rejection description
In this field you can enter a rejection description and a translation of it. If the case type is set to Customer nonconformity, you can enter the customer’s rejection description. By clicking the button Insert phrase ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_add_phrase.png) it is possible to insert different phrases which are registered in the Phrases procedure.By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

#### Part
Here you enter the part number of the product which the claim concerns. You can either enter it or manually select it, or it is automatically entered/completed if you start by selecting a serial number in the Serial number A serial number is a number that is used for traceability for parts on entity level. field. If the part has an active revision, this is automatically entered/completed in the Revision field.
Instead of entering one (1) part number here in the case, you can add more parts to the case in the Parts tab.

#### Name
Here you see the part name.

#### Serial number/Batch
The serial number/batch of the product which the claim concerns, if the customer/supplier can specify it. A validation is made for the customer/supplier and a warning ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/warning.png) is shown if the serial number/batch is not linked to the customer/supplier in the case.

#### Batch number
Here you enter the part's batch number, if such exist for the part. It is also possible to enter a batch number that is not registered.

#### Revision
Here you can enter the part's revision which the cases concerns. The revision is set to the part's active revision when the part number is entered. You can select a different revision here if the customer has a claim regarding an earlier revision.

title: Logging of activities/contacts
content:
### Logging of activities/contacts
In this box you can create own logs in text format. You create a new log entry that will automatically be given date, time, and created by. In the box next to it, you can enter a subject, the log text, and also link files.

title: Logging of e-mail
content:
### Logging of e-mail
Here you can log the correspondence of incoming and outgoing e-mails. You can import and send e-mail from the box.

title: New order
content:
### New order
By clicking the Create new order button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_new.png) on the function menu, a dialog window will open where you can quickly create and link a new manufacturing order or maintenance order to the case. This order will function as a replacement order for the part in the case (if it, for example, should be replaced). The part in the case will be default for the order, but this can be changed to any of the other parts contained in the case. You enter, among other things, a quantity, priority, and finish date for the order. The earliest possible finish date is shown for the quantity you have entered. It is also possible to use a function to check delivery times.
There is also a checkbox where you can choose to open the registration procedure of the order (in cases when you need to continue working on the order there). When you click the Save button in the dialog, the order is created and is opened in its registration procedure (if you chose to activate that checkbox).
By using the Add order to case button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_add_row.png) you can link an already registered manufacturing order or maintenance order.
On a row that you add you also find a button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_more_info.png) which you use to show additional information about the order. For the row you can select if material cost, subcontracting cost, and processing cost, should be charged on the order. If none of the CM The contribution margin (CM) is the difference between the standard price and the sales price., CS, and CP checkboxes are marked on the row, nothing will be charged the customer/supplier for the correction.
A linked order also affects the planned and reported costs of the case.
By clicking the Delete order from case button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_delete_row.png) you can disconnect/unlink an order from the case.
By clicking the Go to procedure button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png), you can via the link go to the registration procedure for the order on the row in question.

title: Part totals
content:
### Part totals
A case can contain multiple parts and the cost can be divided among the parts. Here you can select which part/parts the costs should be displayed for. Use the checkboxes in the Include column to select which parts for which costs should be displayed.

title: Planned costs
content:
### Planned costs
In this box you can modify the planned costs for the case. The costs suggested are determined by the template entered on the header row. In order to calculate the costs, click the button Calculate costs ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_calculate.png) in the toolbar of the procedure.
The planned costs can be of different types. Some activities have a planned time and an hourly cost which gives a planned cost that is totaled on one row. There is a planned hourly cost for the activity. This is entered in the Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Cases procedure.
Other types are linked manufacturing orders and operations with material, subcontract, and processing costs. Together they form a planned manufacturing cost, similar to a pre-calculation. Other costs are loaded from the basic data of the case type. These additional costs can be added, deleted, or modified.
The total time and cost are shown as a total at the bottom of the box.

title: Replacement delivery
content:
### Replacement delivery
If the customer should receive or if the supplier should send a new delivery, it is managed in this box. The Lookup The Lookup feature is a powerful search tool which allows you to search and load information from large registers. You open the Lookup feature by clicking on the dropdown button or by using F4 on your keyboard. function is filtered by the customer’s/supplier’s order. If you enter an order, the correct invoice will be automatically displayed.

#### Customer nonconformity
If the customer should receive a new delivery, you can either create a new customer order in Register customer order procedure or link an existing customer order. Here you can create a link between the replacement order and the case.

#### Supplier nonconformity
If the supplier should send a new delivery, you can either create a new purchase order or link an existing. A link is automatically created between the case and the order.

title: Return
content:
### Return

#### Goods location
Goods location is available for the case type Customer nonconformity. You can enter a goods location in order to indicate where the returned parts have been placed. This is to avoid defect parts being registered in the stock balance.

#### Previously reported quantity
If you have activated the system setting Affect balance for case you can perform stock reporting by linking ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png) to the Direct stock reporting procedure for the case in question. Stock reporting can be made for all case types.
The part's default quantity in the case that is used to report report arrivals or withdrawals on location in that procedure, is calculated as the entered Number of rejections in the case minus Previously reported quantity in the case. In this field you see the previously reported quantity.
By using the button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_more_info.png) next to the field you find a log where you can see information about previous stock reporting items. You find the following information in the log: reported when (date and time), user name, location name, balance change, and batch number or serial number (if the part has traceability).
You cannot delete a case if stock reporting has been made.

title: Return order
content:
### Return order
By clicking the Go to procedure button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png) on the function menu, you can go to the Register return order procedure to register a return order (a purchase order with a negative quantity) based on the case in question.
Information that is automatically loaded from the case to the selection in that procedure is: supplier (supplier nonconformity), parts, purchase order for initial delivery (supplier nonconformity), alternatively purchase order for initial purchase (customer nonconformity, 8D). The case number is entered automatically for the purchase order rows which have been selected for the return order.
When the return order is saved in the Register return order procedure, it will here be shown on a row if you update the case by using the Reload button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_refresh.png) (Ctrl + Shift + R) on the toolbar of the procedure. On this row you then see the information from the return order.
When there is a row here with a return order, you can also use the Go to procedure button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png) to go to the Register purchase order procedure with the return order already loaded.

title: Header row
content:
### Header row
The header row is different depending on the case type you have selected.

#### Case number
This number is unique for each case. You either load the number by using the Lookup The Lookup feature is a powerful search tool which allows you to search and load information from large registers. You open the Lookup feature by clicking on the dropdown button or by using F4 on your keyboard. feature or you enter a new one. If you enter a case number that does not yet exist, you will be creating a new case.
You can link cases together by using the Link the case to other cases ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_test_call.png) button. This can be useful to keep track of cases that are related or where there are dependencies. You can, for example, link multiple customer cases to a supplier case and vice versa, which provides a clear overview.

#### Name
Here you can write a descriptive text as a name. You enter name texts in the company language and they are displayed in the user’s language.

#### Linked cases
If there are linked cases, the button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_connected.png) is displayed to the right of the case number. You can use the button to see which other cases this case is linked to. You can also add cases that should be linked to the active case, or remove existing linked cases.

#### Case type
Here you select case type. The case type that you have set as default in your user account, will be suggested. If you have not configured a default case type there, then the case type you used on the most recent case will be suggested. A few case types are included in new MONITOR systems to use as examples. Other case types that you need must first be registered in the Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Cases procedure. The case type determines prefix, priority, and which fields that will be displayed in the procedure.
By using the Change case type button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_change_record.png) you can change the case type for an existing case.

#### Template
Here you can select a template for the phase/activity and the cost. If someone has already reported the activity or the cost and you change the template, then the other person will get a suggestion to also change template when the reporting is made.

#### Customer/Supplier
If you register a customer nonconformity or an 8D nonconformity, you must enter a customer to which the case belongs. If you register a supplier nonconformity, you must enter a supplier. The case types Internal nonconformity and Own nonconformity type, do not use fields where you should enter customer or supplier.
If the customer/supplier is blocked for registration, a message will appear where you can also see the cause of the block. It is possible to create a case for the customer/supplier. If a notification has been configured for the customer you will see the message/notification, but you can still create a nonconformity for the customer.

#### Priority
Here you see the priority of the case, 1-9. The default priority is determined by the case type's setting in the Basic data – Case procedure. It is possible to change the priority manually. The value can be between 1 and 9.

#### Phase view
Here you see a symbol consisting of arrows, representing how far the case has come based on the status of the phases. Under the Phases/Activities tab you will see the phases and their statuses. A phase can have one of the following status options: Not started, Started, and Finished. The number of phases for a case varies. The phase view shows one arrow per phase in different colors for each status. That way, it is easy to see what the situation is like for the case.
You can see arrows for up to 10 phases. If there are 11 phases or more, you will see a percentage instead, since there is no room for more arrows. E.g. if 3 of 11 phases are finished, the percentage shown will be 27%.
The colors represent the following statuses:
- ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/SubProjects/phase_img_1.png) – the phase is not started.
- ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/SubProjects/phase_img_2.png) – the phase is started.
- ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/SubProjects/phase_img_3.png) – the phase is finished.

title: Documents
content:
### Documents
Under this tab you handle all external and internal documents related to the case. The available documents types depend on the case type selected in the header. You can change the printout date if needed.

title: The Parts tab
content:
### The Parts tab
This tab is used to register multiple parts for the same case. It is also used to enter additional information for these parts.

#### Default
Here you enter which part is the main part in the case. The information entered on this row is reflected in the other tabs in the case.

#### Part
Here you enter the part number of the product which the claim concerns. You can either enter it or manually select it, or it is automatically entered/completed if you start by selecting a serial number in the Serial number A serial number is a number that is used for traceability for parts on entity level. field. If the part has an active revision, this is automatically entered/completed in the Revision field.

#### Name
Here you see the part name.

#### Serial number/Batch
In this field you select the serial number for the product which the claim concerns, if the customer/supplier can specify it. A validation takes place against the customer/supplier and a warning is shown if the serial number is not linked to the customer/supplier in the case.

#### Revision
Here you can enter the part's revision which the cases concerns. The revision is set to the part's active revision when the part number is entered. You can select a different revision here if the customer has a claim regarding an earlier revision.

#### Cause code
Here you enter the cause code provided by the customer in the claim. Rejection codes are handled in the Rejection codes/Error codes procedure. Please find more information about Cause code etc. in the [Basic information](bBasicInformation.htm) topic.

#### Number of rejections
Here you enter the number of rejections that the case refers to. When the case is saved with a number of rejections and part number entered, you can by using the button next to the field go to the Direct stock reporting procedure and have the part number and quantity filled in for withdrawal. The link is only available if the system setting Affect balance for case is set to Yes.

#### Rejection description
In this field you can enter a rejection description and a translation of it. If the case type is set to Customer nonconformity, you can enter the customer’s rejection description. By clicking the button Insert phrase ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_add_phrase.png) it is possible to insert different phrases which are registered in the Phrases procedure. By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about language management for translatable texts.

#### Batch number
Here you enter the part's batch number, if such exist for the part. It is also possible to enter a batch number that is not registered.

#### Customer order number – Replacement delivery
If the customer should receive a new delivery, you can either create a new customer order in the Register customer order procedure or link an existing customer order. Here you can create a link between a replacement order and the case. If you enter an order, the correct invoice will be automatically displayed. The field is only active if the case type is Customer nonconformity.

#### Invoice number – Replacement delivery
Create a link between an invoice number and the case. If you enter an invoice number, the correct customer order will be displayed automatically. The field is only active if the case type is Customer nonconformity.

#### Purchase order number – Replacement delivery
If the supplier should send a new delivery, you can either create a new purchase order or link an existing one. A link is automatically created between the case and the order.

#### Consecutive number – Replacement delivery
Here you enter the consecutive number of the supplier invoice. The field is only active if the case type is Supplier nonconformity.

#### Order number (Initial delivery)
Here you enter the order number of the initial delivery to which the part belongs. The number you enter is validated against the customer in the customer nonconformity.

#### Delivered quantity (Initial delivery)
Here you enter the quantity the initial arrival/delivery consisted of.

#### Delivery date (Initial delivery)
Enter the date when the initial delivery was made.

#### Invoice number (Initial delivery)
Enter the invoice number that the delivery was invoiced with.

#### Purchase order numbers (Initial delivery)
The order number for the initial arrival to which the part belongs. The number you enter is validated against the supplier in the supplier nonconformity.

title: The Parts tab
content:
#### Arrival reported quantity (Initial delivery)
Here you enter the quantity the initial arrival/delivery consisted of.

#### Delivery date (Initial delivery)
Enter the date when the initial delivery was made.

#### Consecutive number (Initial delivery)
Enter the consecutive number that the arrival’s invoice received.

#### Project (Initial delivery)
Here you enter the project to which the initial delivery belongs.

#### Manufacturing order (Initial manufacturing)
If the part is manufactured by you, you can link the manufacturing order information to the case. If the part is delivered to you, you can enter the manufacturing order of the initial manufacturing of the nonconformity part.

#### Operation (Initial manufacturing)
Here you can enter the operation number, if the nonconformity can be traced to a certain operation. The field becomes active when a manufacturing order has been selected.

#### Work center (Initial manufacturing)
Here you can enter the work center, if the nonconformity can be traced to a certain operation.

#### Manufactured quantity (Initial manufacturing)
Here you can enter the manufactured quantity where the initial production of the claimed part took place. This is a numerical field with two decimals. If the part number has been entered you will see the part's standard unit in the field. By default, here is no value in the field. The field becomes automatically filled in with the finished quantity of manufacturing order if it is finished.

#### Manufacturing date (Initial manufacturing)
Here you can enter the finish date when the initial production of the claimed part took place. This is empty by default. If there is a finish date from the manufacturing order, this is filled in automatically.

#### Purchase order (Initial purchase)
The order number for the initial arrival to which the part belongs. The number you enter is validated against the supplier. The field is only active if the case type is Customer nonconformity.

#### Arrival reported quantity (Initial purchase)
Here you enter the quantity the initial arrival consisted of. The field is only active if the case type is Customer nonconformity.

#### Delivery date (Initial purchase)
Enter the date when the initial arrival was made. The field is only active if the case type is Customer nonconformity.

#### Goods location (Return)
Goods location is available for the case type Customer nonconformity. You can enter a goods location in order to indicate where the returned parts have been placed. This is to avoid defect parts being registered in the stock balance.

#### Confirmed rejection
If you realize during the handling of the case that the rejection code or the number of rejections initially entered were not correct, you can change the information in this box. It might for example be a customer who has provided you with information about a certain error or a certain number of rejections. At a later stage, it might be discovered that the error depends on another reason or that the number of rejections was not correct. You can then enter the new information in this box and it will override the information provided initially.
If the rejection code and the number of rejections were correctly entered initially, this box does not need to be used to verify the error.

#### Cause of nonconformity
Here you can choose a rejection code as the cause of the nonconformity in cases when the cause can be linked to such a code.
Here you can also choose a supplier as the cause of the nonconformity in cases when the nonconformity can be linked to a supplier. It can be e.g. a subcontract, a transport damage, or a delivery of incorrect material.
Enter the material's part number if the cause origins from a faulty incorporated material in a manufactured part.
For customer nonconformity or internal nonconformity you can enter a work center or department if the cause can be tied to any of these parties.
You can also enter a cause description and link files.

title: Phases/Activities
content:
### Phases/Activities
In this box you enter information about all planned activities for the case. The default phases and activities depend on the template entered in the header. Some activities are conditional for the specific case. E.g. It might be an activity to return parts to the supplier that you only activate for the specific case.
An activity always belongs to a phase. Phases and activities can be inserted, deleted, and modified after the case has been saved. You can either report the activities in this procedure or in the Tasks view in the Message center (on the title bar of the program window). You can use drag and drop to change the phase order.
With the Insert activity template button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_add_template.png) you can add an activity template in the list. Activity templates are handled in the Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Case procedure.
The following fields must be entered for a phase

#### Dependency types
The following dependency types exist between phases or activities:
Finished – Start
Activity B cannot be started until activity A is finished.
![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/SubProjects/RelationTypeFinishedStarted.png)
Started–Start
Activity B cannot be started until activity A is started.
![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/SubProjects/RelationTypesStartedStart.png)
> Please note! There is a limitation of dependencies, a case can either have dependencies between activities or dependencies between phases.

#### Phase/Activity
Here you can select phases among the ones registered under the Templates/Default tab in the Basic data – Case procedure.

#### Name
You can change the name of the phase.

#### Responsible
Here you see a person default set as responsible according to the settings in the basic data. It is only possible to select users which have the setting Can be set as responsible for activity activated in the Users procedure.
The following fields are shown but cannot be edited

#### Planned time
Here you see the total of planned time from the underlying activities.

#### Planned start date
In this column you see the earliest start date of the underlying activities.

#### Planned finish date
Here you see the latest planned finish date of the underlying activities.

#### Status
This follows the underlying activities:
- Not started – This status is shown if none of the activities has been started.
- Started – This status is shown if any of the activities have been started.
- Finished – This status is shown if all activities have been finished.

#### Reported time
Here you see a total of the reported time from the underlying activities.

#### Actual finish date
Here you see the latest actual finish date of the activities.

#### Print
This checkbox follows the underlying activities. If this Print checkbox is checked for any of the activities, the phase will also be marked. With this checkbox you determine if the activity should be shown on the report.

#### R (Reminder)
Here you determine is a reminder should be sent.

#### C (Charge)
Here you decide if the activity should be charged.

title: Register case
content:
## Register case
In this procedure you register cases. Cases are mainly nonconformities, but there can also be other types of cases. A case can e.g. be a modification of a product or a suggestion of improvement. You can register a case for things you want to follow up on regarding activities and costs.
The case type you select when registering the case can be changed. The case type mainly determines which fields will be visible in the procedure window and the activities that will be suggested. These activities and costs can be changed in the procedure called Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Case.
By configuring some system settings for purchase and manufacturing, you can initiate a registration of a case at rejection in the Receiving inspection procedure and at rejection when reporting manufacturing orders. In that event, the case will be created once you save the rejection. You can then choose to go ahead to that case. A lot of the information in the form is automatically completed.
You can add extra fields for this procedure in the Extra fields procedure. If such fields already have been created, these will be available under the Extra fields tab.
Support for 8D
The case type called 8D Standard makes it possible to apply the 8D method in Monitor ERP. If you have selected the 8D case type, the Header tab will get a different design and contain boxes with all steps included in 8D.
Attach XML file when case is sent via e-mail
If you have customers or suppliers who also use Monitor ERP, you can attach XML files if you send cases as PDF files by e-mail. The setting for this is configured under the Attach XML file button in the Customer register and the Supplier register procedures. To customers you can send confirmations and replies regarding cases. To suppliers you can send claim reports. The customer/supplier then imports the XML files to their cases from the Inbox Monitor-to-Monitor desktop component or by using drag and drop of e-mail or XML file. Read more about [Monitor-to-Monitor](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/M2M.htm).
Read more about [Case management](../../../UserGuide/Using/CaseManagement/CaseManagement.htm) under Using Monitor in the online help function.

title: Stock
content:
# Stock
The Stock module in Monitor ERP contains procedures used for management of parts, requirements planning, inventory, valuation and traceability of parts. This module also contains case management.
Below you find the online help function for all procedures in the Stock module.

title: Activity templates
content:
### Activity templates
Templates
In this box you register different activity templates. For example, templates that can be used to have different activities be performed when a new part is created, a new revision is made for a part, etc. An activity template should consist of different default activities.

#### Number
Here you can see the number for the position of the row. This field is numerical. A new row will by default be assigned the next available number. The table/list is sorted by this column. A number is unique and cannot occur on more than one row in the table.

#### Name
Here you can write a descriptive text as a name. The name text is entered in the company language and is displayed in the user’s language.
By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.
Activities
In this box you select activities to the template that have you selected in the box above. You can also change the order of the activities. The activities which can be selected must be registered in the procedure Activities.

#### Number
Each activity will be given a consecutive number. The first activity is always given number one (1).

#### Name
Here you see the name of the selected activity. However, it is possible to change this name but the field cannot be left empty. We suggest you enter a name which is descriptive of what should be done.

#### Responsible
Here you select a person responsible for the activity. The user linked to the logged-on user is displayed by default.

#### Administrator
The administrator of the part is set as responsible.

#### Comment
Here you can enter a comment regarding the activity. By clicking this button you access a text editor where you can write and format text, insert images and signature, and hyperlinks, etc. When a comment/text exists, the symbol on the button will change from an empty speech bubble ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_no_comment_18x18.png) to a filled speech bubble ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_comment.png).

#### Files
Here you can link external files to the activity. By clicking the Files button, it is possible to link different files related to a comment or an instruction for the record in question. When the setting Automatic printout is available for activation, you can choose to get the linked file automatically printed. Read more in the topic General features about how to link files, automatic printout, and where linked files can be automatically printed. If there are linked files, you will see this symbol ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_file_linked.png) on the button.

#### Due date from registration
Here you enter the number of work days which determine the due date calculated from the registration date.

#### Status
Here you can see the status of the activity. There are three different statuses: Not started (default), Started, and Finished. Finished activities are displayed in green text in the Activity field.

#### Reminder
This setting determines whether or not a reminder will be sent to the person responsible. The purpose is to inform the person responsible that there is an activity to perform. The message contains information about the part and activity in question, and when the activity should be performed. A hyper link to the part is also included in the message. The user in the conversation will automatically be set as the responsible user for the activity. If a reminder/message has already been sent, you see a small symbol of it next to the button.

title: Activity templates
content:
#### Mandatory
Check this box for the activities that should be mandatory to perform.
Things to keep in mind when using activity templates
Values loaded from other places (Finish date and Responsible) are shown in italics. If you manually edit the value for an activity, the italic font is removed and the value must hereafter be changed manually.
A linked value on for example, responsible, can automatically be changed if it is loaded from Seller on the customer. When seller is changed, all linked open activities will be updated.
> Please note! There must be a link between the employee (who is used as seller or administrator) and a user. If such a link does not exist, or if the user cannot be selected as responsible for the activity, then the logged-in user will become administrator when the activity is created via the activity template. If the logged-in user is not allowed to be responsible for the activity either, then the activity will not be created at all.
It is not possible to link values in all templates, but for example in quote and on customer, it is possible.

title: Intervals
content:
### Intervals
The Intervals box is activated if you have selected the Manual interval setting in the Forecast deduction box. Here you can add rows with the intervals which should be used in the marked interval setting.
Tables with examples can be found [here](tForecastDeduction.htm).

#### Period length
Here you enter the length of the period. You enter it in number of weeks. The default option is 1 week.

#### Number of periods
Here you enter how many periods of the entered period length which should be included. The default option here is 4 periods.

title: ABC codes
content:
### ABC codes
ABC ABC codes are used to classify the range of parts by the volumes you sell. The codes are used as a scale for the parts that turn over the most money. The turnover is calculated by multiplying the price of the part by the annual volume. Parts that turn over the most money are called "A-parts", and after that, "B-parts", etc. codes are used to classify the range of parts by the volumes you sell. The codes are used as a scale for the parts that turn over the most money. The turnover is calculated by multiplying the price of the part by the annual volume. Parts that turn over the most money are called "A-parts", and after that, "B-parts" etc.
ABC codes are used in the Volume value analysis procedure in order to calculate and analyze the parts' volume value.

#### ABC code
In this column you can enter the code, it consists of one letter. You can add new codes or edit existing codes. The pre-defined codes in the table below is included in new systems:
| ABC code | Type |
|---|---|
| A | According to selected unit |
| B | According to selected unit |
| C | According to selected unit |
| X | Price is missing |
| Y | Annual volume is missing |
| Z | Unclassified |
> Please note! The last ABC code of the Unclassified type, cannot be deleted.
There can only be one code of the type Price is missing as well as of the type Annual volume is missing.

#### Basic safety time
Here you can enter the basic safety time in number of work days. The basic safety time is used to create a safety stock in number of days per ABC code. The stock level calculation will be simplified if there are basic safety times for the ABC codes.

#### Limit %
Here you enter the limits in percent that apply to each ABC code. The total of the percentage values must be 100. Otherwise, it is not possible to save.

#### Amount limit
Here you can enter the amount limit for the volume value of the ABC code. When the amount limit is reached, the ABC code will be set for the part.

#### Amount limit exception for purchased parts
Here you can enter an amount limit exception that applies to purchased parts. The amount entered in this field overrides the value entered in the Amount limit field.

#### Type
Here you can select among the following types:
- According to selected unit – Classification is made according to percentage or amount limit.
- Price is missing – Gathers parts with annual volume greater than zero but where price is missing.
- Annual volume is missing – Gathers parts that have a price but where the annual volume is zero.
- Unclassified – New, previously unclassified parts, as well as parts where both annual volume and price are missing.
These types can then be selected for the list types Classification in the Volume value analysis procedure.

#### Stock count interval
Here you can enter a default stock count interval in months, for parts with this ABC code. However, the stock count interval can be overridden per part in the part register.

title: Activities
content:
### Activities
Under this tab you add activities or handle existing activities. The activities already included in the system are construction, BOM and routing, pricing, and release.

#### Code
In this column you enter the code you wish to give the activity. All activities must have a unique code.

#### Name
Here you can write a descriptive text as a name. You enter name texts in the company language and they are displayed in the user’s language.
By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

title: Alloy codes/Mark-ups
content:
### Alloy codes/Mark-ups
Under this tab you can enter alloy codes and mark-ups. You can create an own list of alloy codes and keep it updated.
Alloy codes for stainless steel are tradition within certain trades. It is used as an addition to the regular price. The price is updated each month based on the world-market price of alloying metals. Mark-ups can be e.g. environmental mark-ups.

#### Alloy code
Here you enter the alloy code of the additional fee, using a maximum of 10 characters.

#### Name
Here you see/enter the name of the alloy code. By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

#### Price
In this column you enter the price for the alloy code. This price should always be entered in the company currency. A maximum of 6 decimals are allowed.

#### Unit
Here you see/enter the unit in which the alloy code should be measured. You handle the units under the Units tab.

#### Service part
The service part which should be used for the alloy code on the order.

#### Modified
Here you can see which user who most recently modified the alloy code. The date and time when the modification was made are shown in the column to the right.
Under the button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_more_info.png) to the far right, you find a log over all modifications made of the alloy code. Here you see who made the modifications as well as when. You can expand each log record and see what has been changed, the value before and after the modification.

title: CN code
content:
### CN code
Under this tab you enter CN codes, using eight digits, for parts that will be purchased or sold within the EU. These codes are used on Intrastat Intrastat is the system which gathers statistics relating to trade in products within the European Union. Gathering of Intrastat statistics is handled in the same way by all EU member states. reports for export and import to and from EU countries. CN codes are only used within the EU.

#### CN code
If you change an existing CN code, the change will affect all parts for which the code is registered. If you delete the code, it will be deleted from all affected parts.

#### Show
In this column you enter how the CN code should be shown in the report:
- Weight (default) – With this option only net weight will appear in the report.
- Other quantity – This option will only show quantity (other than weight) in the report. Unit for quantity must be selected in the Unit field.
- Weight and other quantity – With this option both weight and quantity (number of pieces) will appear in the report.
- Exclude the code from accounting – A part with this option will not be included in the Intrastat report.

#### Unit
Here you choose unit for CN codes that have to be reported with another quantity in the Intrastat report. If no unit is entered, this CN code is blocked in the Intrastat report.

#### Demander/Authority
Here you decide if the CN code should be included in different sustainability reports or other reports relating to environmental standards. The Demander/Authority available in the dropdown menu must first have been registered in the Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Sustainability procedure.

title: Exposure time
content:
### Exposure time
Under this tab you can register exposure time for parts e.g. according to moisture sensitivity level (MSL).
The list is only visible if the Exposure time system setting is activated under the Stock tab in the System settings procedure.
> If you change the exposure time of an existing code in Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Part, the existing batches do not change. This must instead be changed in the Serial number A serial number is a number that is used for traceability for parts on entity level. list procedure using the Exposure time list type.

#### Code
In this column you enter the code you wish to give the identity. Each identity must have a unique code. (E.g. MSL1.)

#### Name
Here you can write a descriptive text as a name. You enter name texts in the company language and they are displayed in the user’s language.

#### Translations
By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

#### Exposure time
Here you enter, in hours, how long a batch can be exposed before any action must be taken.

#### Notification
Here you enter, in hours, how long in advance you would like to receive a notification informing you that the exposure time is almost up.

title: Forecast deduction
content:
### Forecast deduction
Under this tab you add different interval settings regarding forecast deduction for sales forecasts, which can then be selected for a part when the deduction method Periodic intervals has been selected on the part in the Part register.

#### Default
Here you decide if the interval setting should be default when the deduction method Periodic intervals is selected for a part.

#### Number
A row number for the interval settings. This number be changed.

#### Name
Here you see/enter the name of the interval setting.

#### Translations
By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

#### Date from customer order
Here you select the delivery date the interval setting should use as base on customer order: initial delivery date or current delivery date. The initial delivery date is normally selected (that is, the delivery date promised to the customer) since the customer probably has made a forecast and then placed the order according to the forecast.

#### Deduct excess from previous period
If you check this box, the forecasts will also be deducted for previous periods provided that a customer order exists that exceeds the period's forecast quantity. See examples in the tables below.
| Setting not activated (default) |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Part X | Period 1 | Period 2 | Period 3 | Period 4 | Period 5 | Total |
| Gross sales forecast | 50 | 50 | 50 | 50 | 50 | 50 |
| Customer orders | 20 | 40 | 20 | 85 | 50 | 215 |
| Net sales forecast | 30 | 10 | 30 | 0 | 0 | 70 |
| TOTAL REQUIREMENT | 50 | 50 | 50 | 85 | 50 | 285 |
| Setting activated |  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Part X | Period 1 | Period 2 | Period 3 | Period 4 | Period 5 | Total |
| Gross sales forecast | 50 | 50 | 50 | 50 | 50 | 50 |
| Customer orders | 20 | 40 | 20 | 85 | 50 | 215 |
| Net sales forecast | 30 | 10 | 30 | -35 | 0 | 35 |
| Distributed additional deduction* |   | 5 | 30 | -35 |   |   |
| New Net sales forecast | 30 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 35 |
| TOTAL REQUIREMENT | 50 | 45 | 20 | 85 | 50 | 250 |
> * The forecast for period 2 and 3 has here been redistributed in order to manage the large customer order in period 4.

#### Interval settings
Here you decide if the a forecast calculation should be performed Manually or Monthly. Monthly deductions of forecasts take place using fixed monthly intervals, that is, starting the first of each month. The Intervals box is deactivated if you selected the option called Monthly.

title: Goods type
content:
### Goods type
Goods type Goods type describes what kind of part it is, for example machine parts, electronics, etc. Goods type is printed on shipping documents. is entered for parts in order to clarify what kind of goods it is. The purpose is to be able to declare/present the goods type in connection to transport.

#### Code
Here you enter the code of the goods type. The code is automatically created for new rows and cannot be changed.

#### Name
Here you enter the name of the goods type, using a maximum of 35 characters.

#### Active
With this checkbox you determine if the goods type should be active.

title: ISO codes for units
content:
### ISO codes for units
Here you manage ISO codes for units which can be linked to the units under the Units tab in the procedure.
You can add your own ISO codes and delete the ones you do not use. When you install the system, there are a number of predefined ISO codes.

#### Code
Here you see/enter the ISO code.

#### Name
Here you see/enter the name of the ISO code which is a description of the code. This is normally entered in English.

#### Translations
By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

title: Inspection templates
content:
### Inspection templates
Under this tab you register different inspection templates which can be used for receiving inspection on part. The inspection templates are used to trigger receiving inspection when different nonconformities occur, for example, if a part gets a new revision, if a case is registered for the part, or if previous receiving inspections have resulted in rejected material.
Changes made for inspection templates in the Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. – Part and Basic data – SRM procedures will not affect parts/suppliers which have already been assigned the inspection template in question.
That is, if you have assigned an inspection template to a part and you then make changes to, for example, the frequency for that template in the Basic data – Part procedure, these changes will not affect that part.

#### Template code
Here you enter a code for the inspection template. This code is unique and cannot occur on more than one row in the table.

#### Name
Here you can write a descriptive text as a name. The name text is entered in the company language and is displayed in the user’s language.
By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

#### Included nonconformities
Here you select which types of nonconformities that should trigger receiving inspection. The following options are available:
- New revision – Inspection is triggered if the part has status 5 (New revision).
- Registered case on part – Inspection is triggered if there is a case registered for the part and this case has status 1 – Registered, 2 – Printed, or 3 – Started.
- Rejected quantity on inspection – Inspection is triggered if arrival reporting resulted in a rejected quantity.

#### Active
With this checkbox you determine if the inspection template in question should be active. By checking the box you make the inspection template available to select in fields for Inspection settings in different parts of the system.

#### Level
Here you see the number of the inspection level. This field is numerical and cannot be edited. A new row will by default be assigned the next available number. The table/list is sorted by this column.

#### Number of arrivals
Here you enter the number of arrivals which require receiving inspection. If several levels has been entered in the table, the number shown here is the number of deliveries which should be performed before the inspection template activates the next level.

#### Inspection frequency
Here you enter the frequency of the receiving inspection, that is, how often it should take place. For example, if you have entered 2.00 it means every second arrival will be inspected.

#### Revert back to previous level
With this setting you decide if the inspection template should go back to the previous level if any of the entered nonconformity types has been discovered. This setting is only available if the table contains more than 1 level.

#### No. of inspections after nonconformity
This setting is only possible to edit when Included nonconformities is activated. Here you enter the number of inspections which should be made if a nonconformity has occurred.

title: Other part identities
content:
### Other part identities
Under this tab you can register other part identities, for example ETIM codes.
A few fixed part identities are included in the system for GTIN8, GTIN12, GTIN13, and GTIN14 (Global Trade Item Number), SGTIN (Serial Global Trade Item Number), and Other/No type. These cannot be edited or deleted.

#### Code
In this column you enter the code you wish to give the part identity. Each part identity must have a unique code that can contain a maximum of 10 characters.

#### Name
Here you can write a descriptive text as a name. You enter name texts in the company language and they are displayed in the user’s language.
By using the button Translations ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png) you can translate the text to the different active languages registered in the system. Read more about [language management](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) for translatable texts.

#### Active
Here you determine if the part identity should be active. A part identity is active by default. Then it can be selected for parts in the part register.

title: Package types
content:
### Package types
Under this tab you can register new package types or delete those which should not be used. You can also select which package types should be active.
There are several different package types included in the program.
A package type describes what kind of package is concerned. When a package type should be used in the system, an entered exception code for the package type on the shipping agent in question, will primarily be used, Exception codes are registered under the Exception button on the row. If the shipping agent does not have an exception code entered under that button, the code entered in the Code column on the row will be used instead.

#### Name
In this column you enter the name of the package type.

#### Code
Here you enter a general code for the package type using a maximum of 16 characters.

#### Exception
By using the button Exception ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_more_info.png), you can add shipping agents and their codes for the package type. This is useful if different shipping agents use different codes for this package type. The shipping agent's code for package type can consist of a maximum of 16 characters.

#### Active
With this checkbox you determine if the package type should be active. By checking the box you make the package type available to select in fields for package type in different parts of the system.

title: Part codes
content:
### Part codes
Under this tab you create part codes and names for these. Part codes are then used to group parts in the part register, e.g. in order to divide parts into different qualities, types, variants, etc. Part codes can also be used as a selection term in different lists. You can also delete part codes. A check will then be made to make sure the code is not used, e.g., on any parts, discount categories.

#### Part code
In this column you enter the code for the part. It can consist of a maximum of 10 characters. A code must be entered for each part.

#### Alias for BI
Here you can change the record's alias. This alias is used during data mining from records in the database in Monitor ERP to the database for Business Intelligence. The default value of alias is the same as the record's code/number, but this can be changed.
One of the purposes with alias is to be able to determine for which records data should be extracted to business intelligence. If the alias field is emptied for a record, then no data will be extracted from this record to the database in business intelligence.
Another purpose is to be able aggregate data. If the same alias is used on multiple records, for example customers, then data from these will be merged into a joint record in the database for business intelligence.
You activate alias for BI with the system setting Use alias when exporting to Business intelligence.

title: Units
content:
### Units
Under this tab, you handle the units. Each unit is entered here as an abbreviation, and you can also enter an explanation. In some fields in the system you will only see the explanation of the unit, e.g. under the Alloy codes/Mark-ups tab in the column Unit. The units that exist when you start up the system for the first time are pcs (pieces), kg (kilos), and m (meters).

#### Default
In this column you decide which unit should be default for a new part you register. If the part you register is linked to a part template, this default unit will be overridden by the unit of the part template.

#### Unit
In this column you can enter the abbreviation of the unit, using a maximum of three characters. You can also modify existing units, delete, or add new units.

#### Explanation
In this column you can enter an explanation regarding the unit. In certain unit fields in the system you will only see this explanation since the abbreviations are very short and can be difficult to interpret.

#### ISO code
The unit’s ISO code is configured for the units included from start in a new system. If you add own units you can here choose among a number of predefined ISO codes that are included.
You can also modify, add, and delete ISO codes under the ISO codes for units tab.
An ISO code must be registered for all units when e-invoice is used in the Electronic invoice management (EIM) option.

title: Basic data – Part
content:
## Basic data – Part
In this procedure you add and handle basic data for your parts.
Basic data With "basic data" we refer to the static records in a database, for example parts, customers, users, work centers, etc. is:
- Activities – for a structured way of working with parts.
- Activity templates – for a structured way of working with parts.
- Units – the units that should be used for parts in the system.
- Part codes – used to group parts in the part register, e.g. in order to divide parts into different qualities, types, variants, etc.
- Other part identities – e.g. GTIN8, GTIN12, GTIN13 and GTIN14 (Global Trade Item Number) and SGTIN (Serial Global Trade Item Number).
- CN codes – (goods codes used within EU) and determine how they should be reported.
- ABC ABC codes are used to classify the range of parts by the volumes you sell. The codes are used as a scale for the parts that turn over the most money. The turnover is calculated by multiplying the price of the part by the annual volume. Parts that turn over the most money are called "A-parts", and after that, "B-parts", etc. codes – used to determine how the parts will be classified according to their annual volumes and determine the stock count intervals.
- Alloy codes and Mark-ups – make it possible to update the additional costs of parts.
- Package type Package type describes what kind of package that is used, such as "pallet" for EU pallets, "box" for cardboard boxes etc. – here you register the package types that should be used in the system. The package type describes what kind of package is concerned.
- Goods type Goods type describes what kind of part it is, for example machine parts, electronics, etc. Goods type is printed on shipping documents. – used to declare/present the goods type in connection to transport.
- Inspection templates – used when variable receiving inspection for parts is applied. Here you register inspection templates which you then link to purchased parts in the Part register.
- Forecast deduction – interval settings regarding forecast deduction for sales forecasts, which can then be selected for a part when the deduction method Periodic intervals has been selected on the part in the Part register.
- ISO codes for units – ISO codes for units which can be linked to the units under the Units tab in the procedure.
- Exposure time – exposure times for parts, e.g., Moisture sensitivity level (MSL).

title: Log for part
content:
### Log for part
In this box you see a log after the check is made of the marked parts. If a part cannot be deleted or it cannot be deactivated, you will see row with information about in which registers the part occurs.
By using the Go to procedure button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png) you can via the link go to related procedures for the log item on the row in question.

title: Result
content:
### Result
In this list you see the parts selected to be deleted.

#### Include
Mark this checkbox for the parts you wish to include in the deletion check.
By clicking the Run deletion check on all selected parts button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_run.png) on the function menu, you run a check on the marked parts to see if they are possible to delete or deactivate.
> Please note! Parts that you delete are deleted from the part register. Parts that you deactivate will remain in the part register but will not appear in the Lookup The Lookup feature is a powerful search tool which allows you to search and load information from large registers. You open the Lookup feature by clicking on the dropdown button or by using F4 on your keyboard. feature and you will not be able to register orders for them. In Monitor ERP it is normally not possible to delete old and expired parts if they still have dependencies, for example that they still exist on manufacturing orders. That is why you can deactivate such parts, where the order status is Historical. The actual execution of deletion/deactivation takes place when you save in the procedure.
- Parts which cannot be deleted or deactivated are displayed with an error symbol ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/error.png) after the check has run.
