content:
#### Show in unit for stock count and stock reporting
Here you decide if the unit selected for stock count should be used in the stock value list.

#### Show configured parts
This setting is available if you use the option Product configurator. The setting determines if also configured parts should be included in the list. These parts are then valuated in the same way as other parts according to the available price alternatives.
> For configured parts, the configurations' calculated price is saved in the stock transaction log. This affects the valuation according to FIFO on new reporting items.

#### Current FIFO price
This setting can be activated if the price alternative for purchased or manufactured part is set to FIFO price, and if the balance option selected is historical balance. The price in the lists is shown with the current FIFO price for each arrival that has been added to the total balance at the specified time, instead of the FIFO price which was reported at the specified time. If this setting is activated, the FIFO price in the stock value will take price changes in the stock balance made after the date entered in the selection, into consideration.

#### No. of decimals for price
Enter how many decimals should be used in the price. The default option is 2, but you can select 0 to 6 decimals.

#### No. of decimals for value
Enter how many decimals should be used in the value. The default option is 2, but you can select 0 to 6 decimals.

#### Ignore renamed locations
Can be used in the list type Detailed with location if Historical balance or Last stock count date is selected as balance alternative.
Location names that were modified in Monitor G4 can cause renamed locations to be displayed with a balance in the Detailed with location list type. If you activate this setting, the system will try to identify such name changes and ignore the balance for these locations.

title: Settings – Stock value change/Reconciliation
content:
### Settings – Stock value change/Reconciliation

#### Reconciliation of general ledger
This setting is activated by default if Stock accounting Stock accounting is a standard feature in Monitor ERP. It is used to continuously post all stock transactions in the system. This way the stock value in the Stock module matches the recorded value in the Accounting module. Changes in stock which are due to changed standard prices, direct stock reporting, arrivals and deliveries, stock count differences, nonconformities (cases), etc. will automatically be posted and give a better understanding of changes in stock and the company's gross profit margin in the income statement. and Management accounting Management accounting is an option in Monitor ERP. It is used as a complement to the standard function called Stock accounting. The function means that all transactions on manufacturing orders (WIP value) are posted and transferred to the general ledger in the Accounting module in Monitor G5. The hours worked are recorded in the income statement, and provide a financial follow-up, for example, made per department and cost factor. Calculation differences are posted and these can be followed up per product, per order, etc. This function also contains extended management of cost of goods sold. are applied. With this setting activated, the Booked change and Difference columns are displayed as well as everything relating to bookkeeping.
By not activating this setting, companies which have not activated the Stock accounting or Management accounting can use this list as a basis for the manual recording of the change in stock.

#### Account
Here you enter the accounts against which the reconciliation should be made. This is used when the Reconciliation of general ledger setting is activated.

#### Reconciliation period
Here you enter a date interval for the reconciliation period. This period is by default configured to be the last month. This is done to improve the performance. However, you can change the date interval.

#### Include SO mark-up
With this checkbox you determine if SO mark-up (storage overhead mark-up) should be Included in the reconciliation.

#### Include parts without entered value
With this setting you determine if parts without entered value should be included in the reconciliation.

#### Only show parts with difference
With this setting you determine if only parts with difference should be include included in the reconciliation. This is used when the Reconciliation of general ledger setting is activated.

#### Include not approved journals
With this setting you determine if journals which are not approved should be included in the reconciliation. This is used when the Reconciliation of general ledger setting is activated.

#### Show configured parts
With this setting you decide if configured parts should be included in the reconciliation.

title: Settings – Total by date
content:
### Settings – Total by date

#### Date
With this setting you determine if the parts should be valued to the price that applied on the Log date or at the Actual date. The price for that date is registered in the standard price log in the part register.

#### Price alternative for purchased part
This is always the standard price. You cannot change the price alternative for purchased parts in this list.

#### Price alternative for manufactured part
This is always the standard price. You cannot change the price alternative for manufactured parts in this list.

#### Historical price
Here you determine if the parts should be valued using the historical price. If you do not activate this setting, the parts will instead be valuated according to the current standard price.

#### Include SO mark-up
It determines if SO mark-up (storage overhead) should be added to the parts in the list.

#### Group dates by
Here you decide how the dates should be grouped. The available options are: Day, Week, Month, Quarter, and Year.

title: The Project list
content:
### The Project list
This list is based on records reported for a project in the stock transaction log. You can check the stock transaction log records which have been reported for projects and which are the bases for the balance in the list in the stock transaction log.
Prerequisites:
- You purchase for project and consume/sell for the same project.
- You manufacture for project and sell for the same project.
The list requires an arrival on a project in order for the part to be shown in the list for the project in question. The list does not display an "actual balance" for the part in question, but only what is reported according to the stock transaction for project.
Example: If you purchase 10 pieces for project A, and you consume 10 pieces without a link to a project, this means that the balance is 0. But if you select the list by project A, the list will show a balance of 10 even though the total balance is 0. If you purchase 10 pieces for project B and stock count 5 pieces, it means that the total balance is 5. But if you select the list by project B, you will see a balance of 10 even though the total balance is 5.
If you only have consumption/sales on project, that is, no arrival reporting has been made, you can mark Show parts with negative balance on project to show these parts in the list.
There are procedures where you report items that will affect the balance but where there today is no support for projects, such as e.g. stock counts. If you discover incorrect reporting items, you can correct these in the Direct stock reporting procedure.

title: The Stock value change/Reconciliation list
content:
### The Stock value change/Reconciliation list
In this list you reconcile the stock value with booked balances on stock accounts in the accounting module.
If you have several stock accounts, you should reconcile one stock account at a time and make selections of orders, parts, product groups, part codes, etc. in order to make a correct reconciliation.
If you have installed the option Warehouse, you can choose to show stock values for one or several warehouses. However, booked balances on stock accounts in the accounting are not dependent on warehouse.
The information in the list is displayed for the time period you have selected (for example an accounting period) and is based on part balances, reported prices (standard prices or FIFO FIFO is calculated via the old stock log records existing in the system. All records have a price which is saved during the arrival reporting. However, for a purchase order the price will be updated when the supplier invoice becomes linked to the arrival reported items. This means that the FIFO value can change even though no stock transaction has taken place after the most recent inventory value list was created. Stock count and direct stock reporting will have the standard price as value. Other transactions such as negative reporting of material via manufacturing order, gets the standard price and also affect the FIFO. When FIFO is to be calculated, the part's balance is first checked. Then the program will find as many (positive) transactions as needed to be able to valuate these parts. The most recent transactions will then be used first. Example: If you have a balance of 100 units and the most recent transactions are: first a purchase of 80 units for EUR 10 each and then a purchase of 20 units for EUR 20 each, then the FIFO will be: 80 × EUR 10 + 20 × EUR 20 = EUR 1200, that is EUR 12 per unit. price), price change log, and journals for management accounting. In the list you see (as total for each part) the stock values at the beginning and at the end of the time period, as well as changes made during the time period (both in stock and on stock accounts in the accounting). In the list you can also see differences regarding the stock value changes in the Stock module and the Accounting module. By using this information you can take a closer look at part details and reconcile the transactions that have taken place as well as investigate why the differences occurred.
By marking an order in the Reconciliation box, you see all transactions for the selected part in the Log box. There you can see detailed information about different events for the part during the selected time period. There you also see waring if there are problems regarding journals for management accounting.
In the Summary box you see the stock account's closing balance at the end of the selected time period. The balance is compared with the corresponding value in the stock value list. Any differences are shown in red font. Here you also see to which accounts the summary refer.
Read more about stock accounting in the chapter [Stock accounting and Management accounting](../../../UserGuide/Using/ManagementAccounting/ManagementAccounting.htm) under Using MONITOR in the online help function.
Reconciliation
In this box, the stock values are displayed in the company currency as total per part. Below you find a description of important columns in the list.

#### Opening value
Here you see the part's stock value on the date entered as From date in the settings section under the Selection tab. The stock value corresponds to the loaded value in the Total list if you select the balance alternative Historical balance (actual date), and use the same date as well as activate Historical price for purchased and manufactured parts.

#### Stock value change
Here you see the stock value change between the dates entered in the settings section under the Selection tab.

#### Closing value
Here you see the part's stock value on the date entered as To date in the settings section under the Selection tab. The stock value corresponds to the loaded value in the Total list if you select the balance alternative Historical balance (actual date), and use the same date as well as activate Historical price for purchased and manufactured parts.

title: The Stock value change/Reconciliation list
content:
#### Booked change
Here you see the stock value change in the accounting between the dates entered in the settings section under the Selection tab. The change comes from postings (debit - credit) made on the stock accounts that you have entered under the Selection tab. It is loaded from journals in the stock transaction log and price change log. Only postings that are transferred to the accounting are included in the value, unless you have activated the setting called Include not approved journals under the Selection tab.
This column is shown when the Reconciliation of general ledger setting is activated.

#### Difference
Here you see the difference between the stock value change and the booked change. Any differences are displayed in red font.
This column is shown when the Reconciliation of general ledger setting is activated.
Log
In this box you see detailed information about the transactions from which the stock value derives. This is shown for the part marked in the Reconciliation box. Recorded values on stock accounts from postings are loaded from the logs: Stock transaction log and Price change log. By expanding a row using the button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_drill_down.png) next to the date, you can see all booked postings in detail on the transaction. These log records are the basis for the booked change on the selected part. You cannot expand the row if there are no booked changes. Below you find a description of important columns in the list.

#### Date
Here you see the log date in the affected log.

#### Order number
Here you see the order number from the stock transaction log.

#### Transaction type
For transactions from the stock transaction log, you see the transaction type from that log and not from the posting method. For transactions from the price change log, you see the transaction type "Standard price change".

#### Quantity
For transactions from the stock transaction log, you see the balance change. For transactions from the price change log, you see the balance from that log.

#### Stock value change
For transactions from the stock transaction log, you see the value of the log record as: Balance change x Reported price. These are the same values that can be loaded in the Stock transaction log procedure. For transactions from the price change log, you see the value of the log record as: (New price - Old price) x Balance. These are the same values that can be loaded in the Price change log procedure.

#### Booked change
Here you see any changes from the posting of the log record. The change comes from postings (debit - credit) made on the stock accounts that you have entered under the Selection tab. Only postings that are transferred to the accounting are included, unless you have activated the setting called Include not approved journals under the Selection tab.

#### Difference
Here you see the difference between the stock value change and the booked change. Any differences are displayed in red font.

#### Information
If the difference is zero, "OK" is displayed in green text. If there is a difference, you see the cause of the difference.
Summary

#### Stock value
Here you see the closing stock value on the To date.

#### Account balance
Here you see the closing balance on the stock account on the To date.

#### Difference
Here you see the difference between the Stock value and Account balance. Any differences are displayed in red font.

#### From and To date
Here you see the date that was selected as reconciliation period under the Selection tab.

#### Accounts
Here you see the accounts that were selected under the Selection tab.

title: Stock value
content:
## Stock value
In this procedure you can create lists showing the value of the parts in stock.
You can select which balance you want to use in the valuation of parts in stock. The following balances are available:
- Current balance Current balance is the part balance at this moment on the locations..
- Last stock count date
- Optional stock count date
- Different types of historical balances (these are based on actual date or log date).
You can also decide if parts without balance should be included. You can enter a minimum value per unit for the parts you want to include in the list. Different price alternatives for purchased and manufactured parts are then selected for the valuation, e.g. current standard price or a historical price.
> FIFO FIFO is calculated via the old stock log records existing in the system. All records have a price which is saved during the arrival reporting. However, for a purchase order the price will be updated when the supplier invoice becomes linked to the arrival reported items. This means that the FIFO value can change even though no stock transaction has taken place after the most recent inventory value list was created. Stock count and direct stock reporting will have the standard price as value. Other transactions such as negative reporting of material via manufacturing order, gets the standard price and also affect the FIFO. When FIFO is to be calculated, the part's balance is first checked. Then the program will find as many (positive) transactions as needed to be able to valuate these parts. The most recent transactions will then be used first. Example: If you have a balance of 100 units and the most recent transactions are: first a purchase of 80 units for EUR 10 each and then a purchase of 20 units for EUR 20 each, then the FIFO will be: 80 × EUR 10 + 20 × EUR 20 = EUR 1200, that is EUR 12 per unit. always links withdrawals to arrivals based on log date and not the actual date. This means that the correct stock value cannot be guaranteed based on historical actual date when the price alternative is FIFO.
There are no update options in the procedure.
List types

#### Standard
This list shows detailed information about the stock value for the selected parts. The list can be grouped by part code or product group.

#### Detailed with location
This list shows detailed information about the stock value for the selected parts per location. The list is grouped by location.

#### Detailed with traceability
This list shows the same information as Detailed with location, but also shows information about traceability.

#### Total
This list shows total information about the stock value for the selected parts. The balances and values in the list are also displayed as a bar chart. It can be presented as total by part, by part code, or by product group.

#### Total by date
This list shows total information about the stock value for the selected parts. The purpose is to see how the stock value has changed over time. The balances and values in the list are also displayed as a bar chart. This list is shown as total by date, based on the grouping of dates you select in the next field.

#### Configured parts
This list type is available if the option Product configurator is installed in your system. This list is grouped by part number and displays stock value based on current balances of the selected and configured parts.

#### Stock value change/Reconciliation
In this list type you reconcile the stock value with the booked balance on stock accounts in the accounting.

#### Withdrawn reusable tools
This list type is available if you have installed the Tools & Maintenance option. This list is grouped by part code and displays information about the stock value of the selected tools which are currently withdrawn.

#### Project
This list is based on records reported for a project in the stock transaction log. You can check the stock transaction log records which have been reported for projects and which are the bases for the balance in the list in the stock transaction log.

title: Stock value between warehouses
content:
## Stock value between warehouses
This procedure is part of the option Warehouse. The purposes of this procedure is to valuate parts being transported between warehouses. You acquire parts from one warehouse to another by using customer orders and purchase orders of the type stock order.
When delivery reporting has been made of a stock order for sales but no arrival reporting has yet been made of the linked stock order for purchase, then the delivery reported quantity of parts on the order is considered to be in transit. This quantity does not belong to any warehouse and can for this reason not be valuated in the Stock value procedure. Also the quantity that is subject to receiving inspection in the receiving warehouse is considered to be in transit. This quantity is therefore also included in the stock value between warehouses.
The stock value between warehouses is always a present value. It is not possible to load a historical stock value between warehouses. It is also not possible to update any data in the list. There are no available list types in this procedure.

title: Settings – Internal operations
content:
### Settings – Internal operations
Under this heading you configure settings for valuation of own work and costs for work centers in the calculation of the WIP value.

#### Value of processing
With this setting you determine if reported time or planned time should be used for the valuation of work. By selecting one of the alternatives Reported time or Planned time for reported quantity, you can choose to value work either according to the operation’s actual reported time or according to the operation’s planned time for the quantity that has been reported. If you select Planned time for reported quantity, the setup time will be distributed based on reported quantity.

#### Don't value higher than planned time
If you have selected the option Reported time for the setting above, you can here select to not give a higher value than the value of the planned time. The orders that have a reported time longer than the planned time will be displayed with a warning symbol, and you can also see them under the Warnings tab along with information about the cause.

#### Operation cost
There are two alternatives for type of cost for operations:
- Planned/Reported (default) – The cost for the reported time will be valued at the cost factors that applied at the time of the reporting. By using this alternative, you will get the same operation cost regardless of when the calculation is made (as long as the reported time has not been changed).
- Current – The cost for the reported time is valued at the current cost factors of the work centers. When this alternative is selected you can also choose between the price alternatives Current and Future.

#### Cost factors
Here you select the costs for operations that should be included in the calculation. The costs that are selected in the system setting Default cost factors will here be shown as default.

#### Price alternative
With this setting you decide if current or future prices should be loaded from the cost factors.

#### Calculate with planned setup time (for operations with only reported unit time)
With this setting you include the cost for planned setup time for operations that do not have any setup time reported. This can be used if the operator has included the setup time in the unit time for operations that are reported as finished. The purpose of this setting is to avoid cost differences in cases where the setup time has not been reported. The costs of setup time and unit time can differ, partly due to staffing factors linked to the cost factors, and partly if you have created different cost factors for the work center, one for setup time and another for unit time.
If the operator has reported setup time, the calculation is based on the reported setup time, regardless of this setting.
Example: There is 1 hour of planned setup time and 2 hours of planned unit time registered for an operation. The operator does not report any setup time, but 3,5 hours of actual unit time. If this setting is activated when performing the calculation, the system will calculate 1 hour setup time and 2,5 hours of unit time.

title: Settings – Material
content:
### Settings – Material
Here you configure settings for material in the calculation of the WIP value. Material refers to included purchased and stock driven manufactured parts.

#### Material cost
With this setting you determine which material cost should be used as a basis of the valuation of WIP. It is always the reported quantity being used, but you can select which price to use.
- Current (default)– This alternative will valuate the material cost based on the price alternative that you select in the fields Price alterative for purchased part and Price alternative for stock driven M-part that will be displayed when you select the option Current. The current prices for the parts will then be loaded from the selected price alternatives.
- Reported – With this option the material cost will be valued using the price that applied at the time of the reporting. The price alternatives that have been used are the ones selected in the system settings Price alternative for purchased parts when registering and reporting orders and Price alternative for stock driven parts when registering and reporting orders. By using this alternative, you will get the same material cost regardless of when the calculation of the WIP value is made (as long as the reported quantity is not changed).

#### Include cost for rejection
(Default) Here you determine if the cost for rejections should be included in the WIP calculation.

#### Price alternative for purchased part
With this setting you decide which price to use for valuation of purchased parts. The default price alternative is determined by the system setting Price alternative for purchased parts when registering and reporting orders. Normally, the default price is set to Standard price.
If you select the option Price list you can then choose a price list to use in the field below. You can also choose if Setup price and/or Staggered prices should be included.
If you select the option Supplier price or Future supplier price then you can also select rate type. This can be used in cases where the supplier uses another currency than the your company currency.
You find an explanation of the different price alternatives in this [topic](../../Parts/PartPrices.htm).

#### Price list
Purchased parts will be valuated based on the price list you select here. If you choose a price list in another currency, you will also be able to select Rate type. The price lists must first be registered in the Price lists procedure.

#### Rate type
Here you select which rate type to use when valuing purchased parts based on a price list or a supplier which uses another currency. Rate types must first be registered in the Currencies procedure. The suggested rate type is determined by the system setting Default rate type under the Manufacturing tab.

#### Include
- Setup price – If you activate this setting, it means that when the price calculation of purchased parts is performed, the setup price in the price list/default supplier link will also be included in the calculation. The setup price is displayed under the Direct material tab.
-    
Staggered prices – The price each of purchased parts can be determined by the quantity in the price calculation if staggered prices are applied in the price list/default supplier link. Staggered prices are managed as described below.
If a requirement for the part exists, which is greater than the limit value for a staggered price, then the staggered price will be loaded to the calculation. Otherwise, the regular purchase price for the part will be used in the calculation. In the columns Price each and Staggered qty under the Direct material tab, you will see the staggered price and the staggered quantity. Otherwise, the regular purchase price will be shown and the staggered quantity will be 0 (zero).

#### Price alternative for stock driven manufactured part
With this setting you determine the price alternative that the cost will be valued to for stock driven manufactured parts.
If you select the option Price list you can then choose which price list to use in the field below.
You find an explanation of the different price alternatives in this [topic](../../Parts/PartPrices.htm).

#### Price list
Here you select which price list that should be used to valuate stock driven manufactured parts.. If you choose to use a price list in another currency, you will also be able to select a rate type in the field below. The price lists must first be registered in the Price lists procedure.

title: Settings – Material
content:
#### Rate type
In this field you select the rate type to use when valuing stock driven manufactured parts based on a price list in another currency. Rate types must first be registered in the Currencies procedure. The suggested rate type is determined by the system setting Default rate type under the Manufacturing tab.

#### Price alternative for transfer to stock
With this setting you decide which price to use for valuation of transfer to stock.
If you select the option Price list you can then choose which price list to use in the field below.
You find an explanation of the different price alternatives in this [topic](../../Parts/PartPrices.htm).

title: Settings – Miscellaneous
content:
### Settings – Miscellaneous
Here you configure additional settings for the calculation of WIP value.

#### Valuation time
With this setting you select if you wish to load the current WIP value as for today or a historical WIP value for a date in the past. The historical value can be based on the log date or the actual date of the transactions. If you select one of the alternatives for historical value, you will also be able to select for which date you wish to load the WIP value. Today's date is shown by default.
The historical valuation of WIP takes the order status at the selected time into consideration. E.g. if an order is finished today, but it was not finished at the selected date. This is also possible during historical valuation of current and planned/reported costs. Current costs are the costs that were current at the selected historical date. Planned/reported are the costs that were planned/reported at the selected historical date. In the field Valuation date you select which historical date should apply for the valuation.

#### Show
With this setting you determine which additional columns with different information that will be added to the list. Different columns are available to select depending on the selected list type.

#### Print result tabs
In this field you select which lists from the respective result tabs that will be included when printing to a printer. By default, only the list is printed.

#### Minimum value
Here you select an amount limit for the minimum value in the company currency. If the field is empty, the list will include individual rows for all the selected orders, regardless of how low WIP value each of the orders has. If you e.g. enter 100 as minimum value, all the minor positive amounts up to and including 99 and all the minor negative amounts down to and including -99 will be shown as a total under the headings "Total of small amounts". The small amounts are added to/subtracted from the total WIP value. The purpose of the minimum value is to create a shorter list that does not display small amounts.

#### Show configured parts
This setting is available if the option Product configurator is installed in your system. Here you determine if configured parts also should be included in WIP. You can also choose to only include configured parts.
When a manufacturing order contains a configured part, WIP is calculated as: Quantity x Configuration's saved calculations (instead of Quantity x Standard price).

#### Current FIFO price
This setting can be activated if the price alternative for purchased or manufactured part is FIFO FIFO is calculated via the old stock log records existing in the system. All records have a price which is saved during the arrival reporting. However, for a purchase order the price will be updated when the supplier invoice becomes linked to the arrival reported items. This means that the FIFO value can change even though no stock transaction has taken place after the most recent inventory value list was created. Stock count and direct stock reporting will have the standard price as value. Other transactions such as negative reporting of material via manufacturing order, gets the standard price and also affect the FIFO. When FIFO is to be calculated, the part's balance is first checked. Then the program will find as many (positive) transactions as needed to be able to valuate these parts. The most recent transactions will then be used first. Example: If you have a balance of 100 units and the most recent transactions are: first a purchase of 80 units for EUR 10 each and then a purchase of 20 units for EUR 20 each, then the FIFO will be: 80 × EUR 10 + 20 × EUR 20 = EUR 1200, that is EUR 12 per unit. price and the balance alternative is historical balance. If this setting is activated, the price in the list will be the current FIFO price instead of the FIFO price that was reported at the specified time.

title: Settings – Reconciliation
content:
### Settings – Reconciliation

#### Account
Here you select which account to reconcile.

#### Reconciliation period
Here you enter the start date and end date of the reconciliation period.

#### Only show orders with a difference
With this setting you determine if only orders with difference should be shown in the list. The difference refers to the difference between changes in the WIP value and changes in the booked WIP value.

#### Include not approved journals
With this setting you determine if journals which are not yet approved should be shown in the list. This is used when you want to reconcile the WIP value before the journals are transferred to the accounting.

#### Show configured parts
With this setting you determine if configured parts should be shown in the list. The Product configurator is an option you can add to the system. Please note! The system does not support reconciliation of configured manufacturing orders.

#### Storage overhead mark-up
Here you see storage overhead mark-ups. You can also adjust these mark-ups.

#### Value of processing
With this setting you determine if reported time or planned time should be used for the valuation of work. By selecting one of the alternatives Reported time or Planned time for reported quantity, you can choose to value work either according to the operation’s actual reported time or according to the operation’s planned time for the quantity that has been reported. If you select Planned time for reported quantity, the setup time will be distributed based on reported quantity.

#### Operation cost
There are two alternatives for type of cost for operations:
- Reported (default) – The cost for the reported time is valued at the cost factors that applied at the time of the reporting. By using this alternative, you will get the same operation cost regardless of when the calculation is made (as long as the reported time has not been changed).
- Current – The cost for the reported time is valued at the current cost factors of the work centers.

#### Cost factors
Here you select the costs for operations that should be included in the calculation. The costs that are selected in the system setting Default cost factors will here be shown as default.

#### Value of subcontract
With this setting you determine if reported cost or planned cost should be used for the valuation of subcontract. By selecting one of the alternatives Reported cost or Planned cost for reported quantity, you can choose to value subcontract work either according to the operation’s actual reported cost or according to the operation’s planned cost for the quantity that has been reported. The actual cost is loaded from the supplier invoice that is linked to the purchase order.

#### Planned cost before invoice has been linked
If you have selected the option Reported cost for the setting above, you can here determine that reported subcontracts will be valued using the planned cost according to the purchase order for the reported quantity, until the supplier invoice for the subcontract has been linked. When the invoice has been linked, the subcontracts will be valued to the reported cost according to the invoice. If this setting is not activated, the cost of subcontracts that have no invoice linked to them will be reported as zero.

title: Settings – Storage overhead mark-up
content:
### Settings – Storage overhead mark-up
Under this heading you can enter the general storage overhead mark-up (SO) and subcontract cost mark-up (SC) in percent that will apply in the calculation. The default general mark-up for SC (Subcontracting cost) The SC is a percentage mark-up of the subcontract cost in order to cover all of the costs for the subcontract. Subcontract cost + SC together describe costs for purchase, freight, customs, handling, and stock-keeping. and SO (Storage overhead) The SO mark-up is a percentage mark-up of the material cost in order to cover all the costs for the material. Material cost + SO together describe costs for purchase, freight, customs, handling, and stock-keeping. in percent, and different exceptions from these, if any, must first be registered in the Calculation mark-up procedure.

#### General SC mark-up
Here you enter the general subcontract cost mark-up in percent. This percent value is possible to change.

#### General SO mark-up
Here you enter the general storage overhead mark-up in percent. This percent value is possible to change.

title: Settings – Subcontracts
content:
### Settings – Subcontracts
Under this heading you can configure settings for valuation of subcontract costs in the calculation of the WIP value.

#### Value of subcontract
With this setting you determine if reported cost or planned cost should be used for the valuation of subcontract. By selecting one of the alternatives Reported cost or Planned cost for reported quantity, you can choose to value subcontract work either according to the operation’s actual reported cost or according to the operation’s planned cost for the quantity that has been reported.

#### Planned cost before invoice has been linked
If you have selected the option Reported cost for the setting above, you can here determine that reported subcontracts will be valued using the planned cost according to the purchase order for the reported quantity, until the supplier invoice for the subcontract has been linked. When the invoice has been linked, the subcontracts will be valued to the reported cost according to the invoice. If this setting is not activated, the cost of subcontracts that have no invoice linked to them will be reported as zero.

title: The Direct material tab
content:
### The Direct material tab
Under this tab you will see information about planned and reported quantities, the reported material cost excluding SO, and the reported SO mark-up.
Using the button Go to the level list ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png) on each row, you can link to the material under the Level list tab and see where it is located in the structure.
The tab is similar to the corresponding tab in the Post-calculation procedure. If rejections should affect the post-calculation is determined by the setting Include cost for rejection. In the Post-calculation procedure rejections are part of the cost.

title: The Level list tab
content:
### The Level list tab
Under this tab you find information in all levels in the structure of the selected order and main part. Information is displayed about planned and reported quantity, reported costs, and value of transfer to stock for each included part.
By clicking the button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png) on each row, you can link to the part under the respective tabs Direct material, Order oriented M-parts, or Stock driven M-parts.
The tab is similar to the corresponding tab in the Post-calculation procedure.

title: The List tab
content:
### The List tab
Under this tab the list is totaled by the selected list type. The list Total by order shows information based on the columns you selected under the Selection tab. At the bottom of the list you find a total of the rows (including a total of small items which is not displayed).
Columns considered as self-instructional are not described here.

#### Order number
In this column you see the manufacturing order number of the orders selected to be included in the WIP value.

#### Warnings (W)
If there are warnings after the calculation, a button appears in this column which you can use to go to the warnings list. The warnings you have not clicked on are displayed with a warning sign ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/warning.png) on the button. The warnings that you have clicked are displayed with an exclamation mark ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/warning_validation.png).

#### Status
In this column you can see a symbol representing the status of the order. The status can be 3 (In progress), 4 (Finished), or 5 (Post-calculated), depending on the order statuses selected to be included.

#### Part number
In this column you see the part number of the main part of the order. If there are several main parts, they will be displayed as several rows with the same order number.

#### Total
Here you can see the total of material + subcontract + processing.

#### Transfer to stock
In this column you see the value of already reported quantity with transfer to stock on the last operation. Transfer to stock is calculated as Finished quantity x Price alternative for transfer to stock.

#### Net value
Here you can see the result of Total - Transfer to stock.
The net value is the WIP value of the order, according to the settings configured under the Selection tab.

#### Last reporting date
Here you can see the date when reporting most recently was made.

#### Planned cost
The Planned cost on the order shows the maximum WIP value if everything is going according to plan.

#### Purchase cost
The Purchase cost of the order is shown here (calculated as Standard price × Planned quantity of the main part). It is the value of the future transfer to stock.

title: The Detailed list
content:
### The Detailed list
The data in this list is merged from the tabs Operations and Level list. The list is grouped by manufacturing order, where each part's operation list is shown below its main part in the level list. In the list you see which settings have been configured under the Selection tab.
The list is a document which is suitable to print. The document variant called WIP value, detailed (export) is intended for export to Excel for further processing and analysis.
> You can also create your own variants of the document type in the Document templates procedure. There it is called WIP value, detailed.

title: The Operations tab
content:
### The Operations tab
Under this tab you find information about planned and reported quantities, times and reported costs, and SC mark-ups for operations incorporated in the selected order and main part.
If there is a manufacturing order log for the part, you can see it under the button Manufacturing order log ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_log.png) on the row.
The tab is similar to the corresponding tab in the Post-calculation procedure.

title: The Order oriented M-parts tab
content:

Under this tab you find information about planned and reported quantities, times and reported costs, SC mark-up and the value of transfer to stock for order oriented manufactured parts that are incorporated in the selected order and main part.
If there is a manufacturing order log for the part, you can see it under the button Manufacturing order log ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_log.png) on the row. Using the Go to the level list button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_link.png) on each row you can link to the part under the Level list tab and see where it is located in the structure.
The tab is similar to the corresponding tab in the Post-calculation procedure.

title: The Reconciliation list
content:
### The Reconciliation list
This list is available if you have installed the option Management accounting Management accounting is an option in Monitor ERP. It is used as a complement to the standard function called Stock accounting. The function means that all transactions on manufacturing orders (WIP value) are posted and transferred to the general ledger in the Accounting module in Monitor G5. The hours worked are recorded in the income statement, and provide a financial follow-up, for example, made per department and cost factor. Calculation differences are posted and these can be followed up per product, per order, etc. This function also contains extended management of cost of goods sold.. In this list you reconcile the WIP value with booked balances on WIP accounts the accounting module.
If you have several WIP accounts, you should reconcile one WIP account at a time and make selections of orders, parts, product groups, part codes, etc. in order to make a correct reconciliation.
If you have installed the option Warehouse, you can choose to show WIP values for one or several warehouses. However, booked balances on WIP accounts in the accounting are not dependent on warehouse.
The information in the list is displayed for the time period you have selected (for example an accounting period) and is based on the reporting made on manufacturing orders (operations and material), price change log, and journals for management accounting. In the list you see (as total for each order) the WIP values at the beginning and at the end of the time period, as well as changes made during the time period (both in stock and on WIP accounts in the accounting). In the list you can also see differences regarding the WIP value changes in the Stock module and the Accounting module. By using this information you can take a closer look at order details and reconcile the transactions that have taken place per order as well as investigate why the differences occurred.
By marking an order in the Reconciliation box, you see all transactions for the selected order in the Log box. There you can see detailed information about different events on the order during the selected time period. There you also see waring if there are problems regarding journals for management accounting.
In the Summary box you see the WIP account's closing balance at the end of the selected time period. The balance is compared with the corresponding value in the WIP list. Any differences are shown in red font. Here you also see to which accounts the summary refer.
Read more about management accounting in the chapter [Stock accounting and Management accounting](../../../UserGuide/Using/ManagementAccounting/ManagementAccounting.htm) under Using MONITOR in the online help function.
Reconciliation
In this box, the WIP values are displayed in the company currency as total per order. By expanding a row using the button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_drill_down.png) next to the order number, you can see the WIP value distributed on material, subcontract, processing, and transfer to stock. Below you find a description of important columns in the list.

#### Status
In this column you can see a symbol representing the status of the manufacturing order.

#### Opening value
Here you see the part's WIP value on the date entered as From date in the settings section under the Selection tab. The WIP value corresponds to the loaded value in the Total by order list, if you set the valuation time to Historical value (actual date) and use the same date as valuation date.

#### WIP value change
Here you see the WIP value change between the dates entered in the settings section under the Selection tab.

#### Closing value
Here you see the order's WIP value on the date entered as From date in the settings section under the Selection tab. The WIP value corresponds to the loaded value in the Total by order list, if you set the valuation time to Historical value (actual date) and use the same date as valuation date.

#### Booked change
Here you see the WIP value change in the accounting between the dates entered in the settings section under the Selection tab. The change comes from postings (debit - credit) made on the WIP accounts that you have entered under the Selection tab. It is loaded from logs in all journals except for the invoicing log. Only postings that are transferred to the accounting are included in the value, unless you have activated the setting called Include not approved journals under the Selection tab.

title: The Reconciliation list
content:
#### Difference
Here you see the difference between the WIP value change and the booked change. Any differences are displayed in red font.
Log
In this box you see detailed information about the transactions from which the WIP value derives. This is shown for the order marked in the Reconciliation box. Recorded values on WIP accounts from postings are loaded from the logs: Stock transaction log, Manufacturing order log, and Price change log. By expanding a row using the button ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/button_drill_down.png) next to the date, you can see all postings in detail on the transaction. Below you find a description of important columns in the list.

#### Date
Here you see the log date in the affected log.

#### Transaction type
For transactions from the stock transaction log, you see the transaction type from that log and not from the posting method. For transactions from the price change log, you see the transaction type "Standard price change", if you use standard price in the system or "Post-calculation" if you use FIFO FIFO is calculated via the old stock log records existing in the system. All records have a price which is saved during the arrival reporting. However, for a purchase order the price will be updated when the supplier invoice becomes linked to the arrival reported items. This means that the FIFO value can change even though no stock transaction has taken place after the most recent inventory value list was created. Stock count and direct stock reporting will have the standard price as value. Other transactions such as negative reporting of material via manufacturing order, gets the standard price and also affect the FIFO. When FIFO is to be calculated, the part's balance is first checked. Then the program will find as many (positive) transactions as needed to be able to valuate these parts. The most recent transactions will then be used first. Example: If you have a balance of 100 units and the most recent transactions are: first a purchase of 80 units for EUR 10 each and then a purchase of 20 units for EUR 20 each, then the FIFO will be: 80 × EUR 10 + 20 × EUR 20 = EUR 1200, that is EUR 12 per unit. price. For transactions from the manufacturing order log, you see the transaction type from that log.

#### Quantity
For transactions from the stock transaction log, you see the balance change. For transactions from the price change log, you see the balance from that log as: WIP value's balance - "To stock" balance For transactions from the manufacturing order log, you see the reported quantity.

#### WIP value change
For transactions from the stock transaction log, you see the value of the log record as: Balance change x Standard price or Reported price if you use FIFO. These are the same values that can be loaded in the Stock transaction log procedure. For transactions from the price change log, you see the value of the log record as: (New price - Old price) x (WIP value's balance - "To stock" balance). These are the same values that can be loaded in the Price change log procedure. For transactions from the manufacturing order log, you see value of the log record. The value depends on the settings configured under the Selection tab for internal operations and subcontracts.

#### Booked change
Here you see any changes from the posting of the log record. The change comes from postings (debit - credit) made on the WIP account that you have entered under the Selection tab. Only postings that are transferred to the accounting are included, unless you have activated the setting called Include not approved journals under the Selection tab.

#### Difference
Here you see the difference between the stock value change and the booked change. Any differences are displayed in red font.

#### Information
If the difference is zero, "OK" is displayed in green text. If there is a difference, you see the cause of the difference.
Summary

#### WIP value
Here you see the closing WIP value on the To date.

#### Account balance
Here you see the closing balance on the WIP account on the To date.

#### Difference
Here you see the difference between the WIP value and Account balance. Any differences are displayed in red font.

#### From and To date
Here you see the date that was selected as reconciliation period under the Selection tab.

#### Accounts
Here you see the accounts that were selected under the Selection tab.

title: The Stock driven M-parts tab

title: WIP value
content:
## WIP value
In this procedure you can calculate the value of the work in progress (WIP), that is, the value of manufacturing orders in progress. The report can be used e.g. as a basis when recording the WIP value in the accounting in connection to monthly or annual accounts.
You can calculate the WIP value as a situation report for today or for a selected time in the past. You can also make different choices for how to value the components of the WIP value, that is, how to value material, subcontract, and work. You can also take different price alternatives into consideration for parts, and consider cost factors for work centers.
With different selections and by choosing order status 3 to 5, you can determine which manufacturing orders to be included in the WIP value. The information of the WIP value is based on parts, manufacturing orders, and the associated reporting logs. If you use the Tools & Maintenance option, you can choose to include tools in the calculation. All the values and prices are displayed in the company currency in the procedure.
The procedure is similar to the Post-calculation procedure having the same tabs; Direct material, Order oriented manufactured parts, and Stock driven manufactured parts, Operations, Level list, and Warning list. This division is useful when analyzing details in the WIP value. One thing that differs from the Post-calculation procedure is that the WIP value is always displayed for the entire order quantity. The Post-calculation can display all the values/costs either per unit or total for the entire order quantity. Another thing that differs is that there is no update option of the WIP value.
> FIFO FIFO is calculated via the old stock log records existing in the system. All records have a price which is saved during the arrival reporting. However, for a purchase order the price will be updated when the supplier invoice becomes linked to the arrival reported items. This means that the FIFO value can change even though no stock transaction has taken place after the most recent inventory value list was created. Stock count and direct stock reporting will have the standard price as value. Other transactions such as negative reporting of material via manufacturing order, gets the standard price and also affect the FIFO. When FIFO is to be calculated, the part's balance is first checked. Then the program will find as many (positive) transactions as needed to be able to valuate these parts. The most recent transactions will then be used first. Example: If you have a balance of 100 units and the most recent transactions are: first a purchase of 80 units for EUR 10 each and then a purchase of 20 units for EUR 20 each, then the FIFO will be: 80 × EUR 10 + 20 × EUR 20 = EUR 1200, that is EUR 12 per unit. always links withdrawals to arrivals based on log date and not the actual date. This means that the correct stock value cannot be guaranteed based on historical actual date when the price alternative is FIFO.
List types

#### Total by order | product group | project | customer
The list in the WIP value procedure is shown according to the total of the selected list type. The list type "Total by order" shows the most information, and is based on the columns you have selected to add in the list. These are added under the Selection tab.

#### Detailed
The data in this list is merged from the tabs Operations and Level list. The list is grouped by manufacturing order, where each part's operation list is shown below its main part in the level list. In the list you see the settings that have been configured under the Selection tab.
The list is a document which is suitable to print. The document variant called WIP value, detailed (export) is intended for export to Excel.
> You can also create your own variants of the document type in the Document templates procedure. There it is called WIP value, detailed.

title: Getting started
content:
# Getting started
Welcome to Monitor ERP! This section of the online help is intended for those of you that are new users of the ERP system. Monitor ERP is primarily used as a program installed in Windows.
The program is also available as a mobile client, Monitor Mobile, which you can run in a browser or in an app for Android and IOS. Monitor Mobile is ideal for use in warehouses. Here you can read about the [user interface](../Interface/Interface.htm) and different [functions](../GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm) in the program and about [Monitor Mobile](MobileClient.htm). If you are a system administrator you can read about how to [configure](../InstallConfig/Configuration.htm) Monitor ERP.
Before you start your training in the ERP system and before going live, there are different default settings which need to be controlled and possibly changed. Different basic data should also be registered. If the company is converting from Monitor G4, all data will be included, except for certain basic data which needs to be registered again. If the company changes from another ERP system to Monitor ERP you can import parts, customers, and suppliers from your old ERP system. The work regarding basic data needs to be performed before you can create inquiries, quotes, different orders, etc.
Read more about the basic data you normally should register in the [Basic data and settings](../Using/RegisterBasicData/BasicDataSettings.htm) topic.
In the online help function you can read more about [order flows](../Using/Flows/OrderFlows.htm), [how to use MONITOR](../Using/UsingMONITOR.htm), and [options](../Options/Options.htm). There are different order flows you need to have knowledge of to understand how uou work with inquiries, quotes, and different orders in Monitor ERP. These Monitor ERP options are purchased separately.
> The system administrator must register users and also needs to configure different parts of the system before you can start using Monitor ERP. When you register new users, the Force password setting is activated. This settings requires you to enter a password of a certain length and complexity for the user. You can read more about how the password policy and multifactor authentication (MFA) work in the [Security settings](../../GeneralRegisters/BasicSettings/SecuritySettings/wSecuritySettings.htm) section.

title: Monitor Mobile
content:
### Monitor Mobile
A mobile client, Monitor Mobile, is provided with Monitor ERP. This can be run in a regular browser or as an app on Android or IOS. Monitor Mobile has a clear focus on what is most important for the mobile work flow, quick and easy reporting and a reduced need of printouts. Before using Monitor Mobile, Monitor ERP web server must be installed, and a few settings must be configured for those who are going to use Monitor Mobile.
> You can read more about the procedures and other features in the online help for Monitor Mobile which is available in [English](https://help.monitor.se/en/monitor_g5_web/latest/Content/Topics/Home.htm) and [Swedish](https://help.monitor.se/sv/monitor_g5_web/latest/Content/Topics/Home.htm).
Settings on user
Settings which need to be configured by the administrator under the Security tab in the Users procedure in the Windows client.
![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/UserGuide/SettingsWebUser.png)
- Activate the Allow login to Monitor Mobile setting. When the setting is activated, one of the following settings must also be entered.
Allow login to Monitor Mobile
- Enter a password in the Password field. The password is then used when logging into Monitor Mobile.
- Link an account in Windows to the user with the Windows account setting. Then you do not have to enter a password in the password field. In this case, the Windows account password is used when logging into Monitor Mobile.
Installation of web server for Monitor Mobile
To use Monitor Mobile and the app, the Monitor ERP Web server must be installed in your network. If your IT department or your IT supplier should handle the installation, you find an installation guide [här](../InstallConfig/InstallMONITORWebServer.htm). If you need new installation files, you can contact the Monitor Support Center by phone: +46 650 766 03 or by e-mail: support@monitorerp.com The installation of the web server can also be performed by a technician from the Monitor Support Center.
Web browser
Monitor Mobile can be run on a modern web browser with support for HTML5.
You get the address to the web server by your administrator. When you have entered the address in the web browser, a login page is shown. There you enter your user name in Monitor ERP and the password supplied by your administrator. Alternatively, it is the same password you use for your Windows account.
![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/UserGuide/WebLogin.png)
App for Android and IOS
You can also run Monitor Mobile as an app on smartphones and tablets. There is support for Android and IOS. You can download the app from Google Play, where it's called Monitor Mobile, or from Apple App Store where it’s called Monitor G5.
![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/en-us/Content/Resources/Images/UserGuide/MONAppG5.png)
When you start the app for the first time you are directed to the page for settings. There you enter the URL (web address) to the web server and you can choose if notifications should be displayed on the unit. You get the information about the web server's URL from your administrator.
Procedures in Monitor Mobile
Monitor Mobile client currently contains the below procedures that are suitable for use on smartphones and tablets. You have the same user rights in these procedures as you have in the corresponding procedures (and warehouse) in the Windows client.
Manufacturing
- Pick list A pick list is a list of parts/products which should be picked from stock for a manufacturing order or a customer order.
Purchase
- Report arrival
- Approve purchase order
- Authorize invoice
- Receiving inspection
- Undo arrival reporting
Sales
- Customer list
- CRM view
- Report delivery (pick list)
Stock
- Part list
- Stock count
- Stock count in list
- Create stock count list
- Move stock balance
- Priority plan – Stock
- Direct withdrawal
- Direct arrival
- Register case
- Case list
Time recording
- Attendance list
- Recording terminal
Accounting
- Signing payments
> You can read more about the procedures and other features in the online help for Monitor Mobile, which is available in [English](https://help.monitor.se/en/monitor_g5_web/latest/Content/Topics/Home.htm) and [Swedish](https://help.monitor.se/sv/monitor_g5_web/latest/Content/Topics/Home.htm).

title: Monitor BI
content:
## Monitor BI

#### Smarter decisions with clear visualizations
Monitor BI is a function that converts your company’s data into valuable insights. With this function you get the tools you need to simply and effectively analyze data, create compelling visualizations, and make smarter decisions.
In Monitor BI there is a wide selection of preinstalled dashboards and an editing feature which enables you to create new dashboards and customize existing dashboards.

#### Why choose Monitor BI:
- Gathers data in one place
- Create dashboards and KPIs
- Web-based
- Standard in Monitor ERP

On [this](https://help.monitorerp.com/en-monitor-bi/sv-se/Content/Topics/GettingStarted.htm) page, you can read more about the requirements and recommendations and what you need to do before you log into Monitor BI for the first time.
> Monitor BI has its own online help site, please click [here](https://help.monitorerp.com/en-monitor-bi/sv-se/Content/Home.htm) to access it.

content:
### 设置
通用的

#### 计算方式
通过此设置，你可以确定如何执行计算。手动输入 默认已选择。如果你选择 发票日志 你输入的选项是计算应基于多少个月的销售（发票日志基于开票日期）。在此字段下一个你会看到一个要素，它确保结果总是相当于至一（12 个月）的销售。如果你4输入4 个月，则要素为 3。如果你24输入4 个月，则要素为 0.5。加载的第一个月是时间后退第一个完成的月。然后按相反的按时间排序加载月。
例如：
今天的日期是2018年一月31日。如果你4 个月，则会加载 2017年九月至十二月的销售。

#### 合计自所有仓库
此设置仅在以下情况下可用： 发票日志 选项在上面设置中已选择。通过此复选框，你可以决定是否将全部仓库的日志都被用于在合计中。数据的保存不此设置的影响，因为保存总是保存到你使用该程序的仓库中。

content:
## 计算年度预算

如果已选择年的预算记录不存在，则会已创建一条记录。否则，将已更新当前年度。当你保存预算时，该组件的以下内容将已更新：数量、备选价格、价格和预算图表。

若你已选择使用该部分的预算图表，则主要使用已选择年已已登记的数据。其次，将使用上一年的预算图表。第三，采用平均分配，即预算图表0（0）。

title: 设置–通用
content:
### 设置–通用

#### 保存到
不应用至 负荷 列表类型。通过此设置，你可以决定你保存到的内容： 年度用量 或者 年度用量, 当前节拍。后者选项仅在你已激活了 以当前节拍显示年度预算, 年度用量和订单数量 系统设置.

#### 小数位
这里的默认选项是 2 位小数。可以使用 0在中间8 位小数。

#### 成本要素
应用至列表类型： 负荷， 模拟。在这里你选择应该被用于在计算中的工序成本。系统设置中已选择的成本 默认成本要素 将在这里显示为默认。

#### 包括运输成本
应用至列表类型： 计算年度用量 - 详细， 负荷， 模拟。通过此复选框你决定是否应包含运输成本。如果你选中了此框，则运费将与准备成本一样多。

#### 包括仓储费用加成
应用至列表类型： 计算年度用量 - 详细， 展开， 模拟。通过此复选框，你可以确定仓储费用加成（仓储费用加成）是否应被用于在计算中。

#### 包括仓储费用加成
应用至列表类型： 计算年度用量 - 详细， 负荷， 模拟。通过此复选框，你可以确定是否应在计算中包含外协成本加成（外协费用加成）。对于外协，仅显示成本。准备成本和单位成本的已计算方式与其它工序类似，同时考虑订单数量。如果你已选择含外协成本加成，则会根据每个部分自己的的加成进行已添加。

#### 回退数量
不应用至列表类型： 更新年度用量 和 重置年度用量。如果某个组件的订单数量缺失，你可以在此处输入计算时将使用的回退数量。

#### 考虑最大数量
应用至列表类型： 负荷， 模拟。在这里，你可以决定最大数量是否应覆盖订单数量，即最大数量是否低于订单数量与非0。

#### 显示未更改0记录
应用至 更新年度用量 列表。在这里，你可以决定是否你数量0的组件显示为两者旧的和新数量。

#### 显示0记录
应用至列表类型： 更新年度用量， 展开， 负荷。通过此设置，你可以决定结果为 0（0）的组件是否应显示并可更新。

#### 预选"包括"
不应用至 模拟 列表类型。此设置确定或不质检由所有的默认行的“包括”框。

title: 设置–载入年度用量自
content:
### 设置–载入年度用量自
在此表格中，你可以输入应从哪里加载年度用量计算数据。你可以在同一次计算数据负荷中混合来自不同登记的数据从。
你标记 包括 并输入 从 和 到 应加载数据的间隔日期数，以及 要素 用于向上调整。对于年度用量和年度预算，你不输入任何日期间隔。
仅当你已激活系统设置时，当前节拍的行才可可用 以当前节拍显示年度预算, 年度用量和订单数量。
如果你选择不此处包括任何行，则会加载手工更改日期的列表。然后，两者屏幕上将显示相同的值 旧数量 和 新数量 列表中的列。

#### 储备订单数量根据
如果你在上面表格中已选择包括 储备客户订单，此设置变为可用。这决定了储备订单应该如何显示：根据 剩余数量 或根据 订购数量。

#### 预算自年
如果你在上面表格中已选择包括 年度预算 或者 年度预算, 当前节拍，此设置变为可用。这决定了从哪年开始加载预算。

#### 合计自所有仓库
通过此设置，你可以确定公司中已登记的全部可用仓库或不都应合计在列表中。

title: 设置–其它
content:
### 设置–其它

#### 分组总时间由
在这里你可以选择工作中心的负荷时间是否应按以下方式已分组 工作中心 或者 部门。该设置决定是否应在列表的柱状图中每工作中心或每部门已呈现时间。

title: 设置–价格类型
content:
### 设置–价格类型
这些设置决定应显示采购件、生产件和服务的价格。如果你为任何设置选择了价格列表选项，则其低于的字段将变为可用。在那里可以选择要应用的价格列表。如果你已选择了供应商价格或其他货币的价格，则你可以选择汇率类型的字段也将变为可用。

title: 设置–重置年度用量
content:
### 设置–重置年度用量

#### 预选“包含”
此设置确定默认情况下是否应为列表/结果中的所有行选中“包含”框。

#### 显示零体积的组件
通过此设置，你可以确定是否仅年度用量0的组件显示在列表中。

title: 设置 - 结构展开的条款
heading_path: 设置 - 结构展开的条款
content:
### 设置 - 结构展开的条款
你在此查询有关如何输入备用物料清单 (BOM) 和工艺路线数据的设置。展开过程中会考虑这些条款。例如，如果你在BOM 与工艺路线中为某个客户已选择了一物料应替换另一种物料，然后选择该特定客户号，那么你将在计算中获得另一个BOM 与工艺路线结构。

title: 年度用量标签页
content:
### 年度用量标签页
之后计算 展开 或者 模拟 列表，此标签页将可用全部已选择的主要的组件和展开时发现的合并组件。你可以修改新数量，还你选择要将哪些组件的新数量已保存到年度用量中。如果你已经执行了模拟，则不保存。

#### 新数量
在此列，你可以看到全部结构爆炸合计所你的数量。一个组件可以从包含它的多个产品中获取其数量。你可以在列中更改新数量。

#### 选择
在这里你可以确定在保存你是否应该将组件的新数量已保存到年度用量程序。

title: 列表计算年度用量 - 详细
heading_path: 列表计算年度用量 - 详细
content:
### 列表计算年度用量 - 详细
此列表类型是两个列表的组合，称为 更新年度用量 和 展开。该列表列出了主要的组件的年度用量。
负荷列表之后，你查询你处于一种模式，在这种模式下， 标准 框可以修改新数量和订单数量，还可以选择要包括在计算中的行。
这 年度用量的最近一次重置 和 年度用量的最近一次更新 列（通过单击 更多信息 按钮 ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/button_more_info.png) 在里面 标准 框）可让你对前道重置和计算中的组件进行排序、选择和排除。

content:

title: 展开列表
content:

负荷列表之后，你查询自己处于你修改数量和订单数量的模式，还可以选择要包括在计算中的行。如果该行有数量，你可以选择将包括计算。

计算完成之后，标签页 年度用量 打开。你可以在那里看到已选择组件。你可以在这里修改 新数量。列 保存 被默认已选择并且新数量将被已保存为该组件。
在下面 警告 标签页，你会看到计算运行之后出现的警告（如果有）。

content:
### 负荷列表

之后计算， 负荷 列表打开。这里可以更改每个工作中心的准备时间、单位时间、时间合计和工时。你可以选择你包括的工作中心并将值保存到每个工作中心。然后，这些已保存的值可以显示在例如 年度用量 列表中 工作中心列表 程序。

content:

title: 模拟列表
content:
### 模拟列表
这是一个不更新的列表。它用于在同一次运行中获得结构展开和负荷计算。例如，能够模拟生产特定数量的复杂/复合产品已创建多少原材料和多少负荷。该模拟未保存。你可以使用按钮开始结构展开 开始计算 ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/button_run.png) （Ctrl + 提醒）在程序的工具栏上。
结构展开之后，标签 年度用量 和 负荷 出现。你可以在此查看工作中心的为组件的年度数量。

title: 更新年度用量列表
content:
### 更新年度用量列表
此列表类型加载主要的组件的年度用量已计算数量。从你已选择的日期间隔载入年度用量自数据，然后乘以要素。如果你要负荷3 个月的消耗，你将该值乘以四（要素= 4.00）以获得年度用量。
该列表可用于人工的更新年度用量，或通过选择表格中的内容来计算新数量 载入年度用量自 在设置框中。

#### 新数量
你可以在此列中更新组件的数量。下一个列的不同数量显示 新数量 − 旧数量。当你更新此列时， 新值 列也将会已更新。该值由零件数量乘以零件价格得出。

#### 保存
在此列中你可以决定你保存哪些行。

title: 负荷标签页
content:
### 负荷标签页
之后计算 负荷 或者 模拟 列表，此标签页显示包含全部受影响的工作中心。负荷是根据订单数量来已计算的。这样，准备时间的编号就会正确。
对于外协，仅显示成本。准备成本和单位成本的已计算方式与其它工序类似，同时考虑订单数量。如果你已选择含外协成本加成，则会根据每个部分自己的的加成进行已添加。如果你选择包括运输成本，则运费将与准备成本相同。

#### 准备时间
你在此列中看到的准备时间是基于设置编号x BOM 与工艺路线的准备时间已计算的。

#### 单位时间
你在此列中看到的单位时间是基于组件数量x BOM 与工艺路线的单位时间已计算的。

#### 时间合计
时间合计为准备时间+单位时间。

#### 成本
成本已计算为时间合计x你在“选择标签页下选择的成本要素。这显示了该组件的年度成本。

#### 工时
工时是基于准备和单位的人员配备要素的单独字段已计算的。主要使用来自BOM 与工艺路线中的工序的值，其次使用来自工作中心的值。每个操作的单位时间乘以单位时间的人员配备要素，准备时间的合计乘以准备时间的工时要素。然后将已添加在一起得到合计时间。

#### 包括
标记 包括 保存当你在程序中保存时，应节省时间和成本的工作中心的复选框。在模拟列表类型中，此列不可用，并且你不能保存。

title: 结果标签页
content:
### 结果标签页
在你结构展开运行之后，将显示此标签页 计算费用 列表。列表显示了展开时发现的已选择主要的组件和合并组件。该列表分为组件信息、不同合计（费用等）和计算基础。此计算基础显示每组件在计算之前输入的数量的费用。在列表中你还可以看到已计算费用的新数量。

title: 计算年度用量
content:
## 计算年度用量
在此程序中，你可以重置，计算和保存已选择组件的年度。
数据可以以不同的方式加载，并且可以保存为年度用量或年度用量, 当前节拍。程序中的每个计算类型都分为不同的列表类型。
在设置框中你选择年度用量的加载位置、展开条款以及价格类型。你程序通过 Monitor 代理程序 选项。
列表类型

#### 更新年度用量
此列表类型加载主要的组件的年度用量已计算数量。该列表可用于人工的更新年度用量，或通过选择表格中的内容来计算新数量 载入年度用量自 在设置框中。

#### 计算年度用量 - 详细
此列表类型是两个列表的组合，称为 更新年度用量 和 展开。该列表加载了主要的组件的已保存年度用量，下一个，你开始结构展开计算，订单计算包含/合并组件的年度。
在此列表中，你还可以看到每工作中心或部门的图表中的准备时间和单位时间。

#### 展开
此列表类型加载已保存的年度用量，你可以在列表中运行结构展开计算，订单计算包含/合并组件的年度。

#### 负荷
此列表类型加载已保存的年度用量并分析在不同工作中心订单这些产品需要多少生产产能。然后可以将其已保存为每个工作中心的年度用量。
> 请保持，结构组件将被展开，使得包括/合并的组件也具有年度用量。如果在选择添加你/合并的组件，这意味着合并组件的体积将加倍。

#### 模拟
此列表类型不更新。此列表类型用于在同一次运行中获取展开和负荷计算。例如，通过这种方式，你可以模拟生产x件复杂/复合产品将消耗多少原材料以及已创建多少负荷。该模拟未保存。

#### 计算费用
此列表类型用于基于已选择的采购件体积和价格类型来计算和分析采购费用及加价。在列表中，你可以基于对列表和数量你的选择来运行结构展开计算。在结构展开时，将基于数量已计算每个采购件组件的费用。
年度用量合计计算每个组件每类型的合计费用。此外，还已计算订单编号、包装数量和已计算体积的公斤编号。

#### 重置年度用量
此列表类型用于将已选择组件的年度用量设置0。
选择列
在列表程序中，始终有一个名为选择的标签页，您可以在其中选择数据库中不同间隔的数据记录。然后使用程序工具栏中的载入按钮![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/button_display_list.png)加载数据记录。
在程序后台的选择行下，您可调整位于选择标签页每种列表类型应具有的选择行。在列表类型字段中，您可选择要自定义选择行的列表类型。
一张表显示可以选择的选择行，一张表显示已选定的选择行。您可通过使用鼠标指针拖放来添加、删除或移动选择行。
使用保存按钮![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/button_save.png)保存选定的选择行。
在[选择](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/Selection.htm)主题中阅读有关此内容的更多信息。

title: 设置
content:
### 设置

#### 小数位
在这里你可以输入新价格中应已保存/管理多少位小数。默认选项为 2 位小数，最大为 5 位小数。

#### 预选"保存"
通过此复选框，你可以决定是否在列表中默认已选择“保存” 。

#### 保存小于等于0 的均价
如果你激活设置预选"保存"，此设置也将被已激活。但默认下不激活由此设置。

#### 预选"包括"
通过此复选框你可以决定是否默认已选择全部到货。

#### 包括偏离采购价格
此设置默认激活由。在此列中，你可以确定哪些偏差行应被用于在平均价计算中。复选框 我 然后这些行上会默认默认（包括）。
如果一行的购买价格是小于（平均价值-标准差）或大于（平均价值+标准差），则认为该行的采购价格有偏差。
当列表中的采购订单行有偏差的采购价格时，全部信息均会显示在 红色的 行上和一个警告符号 ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/warning.png) 显示在列中 新平均价 组件。

#### 加权价格
此设置决定在平均价计算期间是否应使用加权价格。如果上面设置被激活，则此设置被已激活， 包括偏离采购价格，也已经已激活。订单基于加权价格计算平均价价格，还必须包含采购统计中存在偏差的采购价格的行。这意味着加权价格考虑每个采购件的体积，与非仅采购价格本身。请参见低于的例如：
|   | 数量 | 单价 | 合计的 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 采购1 | 10 | 500 | 5000 |
| 采购2 | 2 | 600 | 1200 |
| 采购3 | 3 | 500 | 1500 |
| 合计的 | 15 | 1600 |   |
平均价：1600 / 3 = 533.33
加权价格：500 x 10 / 15 + 600 x 2 / 15 + 500 x 3 / 15 = 513,33

#### 准备价格
默认下未检查此设置。此设置决定准备价格是否应被用于在计算中。如果基于采购统计进行计算，则准备价格将包含在订单行中。此准备价格是从发票日志中加载的。如果平均价基于供应商价格，则供应商链接上的准备价格将被用于在计算中。当平均价基于最近采购价或平均采购价时，此设置不应用，因为准备价格总是被用于在这些价格的计算中。

#### 折扣
默认下未检查此设置。此设置确定计算平均价时是否应从单价中已扣减折扣。如果基于采购统计进行计算，折扣将从订单行上的单价中已扣减。此折扣是从发票日志中加载的。如果平均价是基于供应商价格的，则在计算时将从单价中已扣减供应商链接上的折扣。当平均价基于最近采购价或平均采购折扣时，此设置不应用，因为在计算这些价格时总是会已扣减折扣。

#### 到货日期
你可以在此处选择“自日期”和“至日期”。然后基于此期间的购买情况进行计算。如果你离开 从 如果字段空 了,然后后退的时间就无限制.如果你离开 到 字段空，表示今天的日期。

#### 采购订单
在输入你订单计算该组件必须存在的最小采购订单数量。如果采购订单数量低于此数量，然后 否到货报告时的备选价格 用来代替。你还可以输入最大采购订单数量。

title: 计算订单数量
content:
## 计算订单数量
此程序用于计算零件的订单数量。目的是计算一个能够最小化库存和采购成本的数量。该数量稍后将用于需求计划和计算。计算订单数量可以从以下几点得出：
1. 威尔逊公式
2. 每年订单数量
3. 零件最小数量
4. 最小消费
5. 最大消费
根据你配置不同设置的方式，计算根据以下原则进行：将选项 1、2 和 3 中的值与选项 4 或 5 进行比较。若1、2、3中值是小于方案4，则根据方案4计算。若1、2、3中值是大于方案5，则根据方案5计算。
这 订单数量 和 订单数量, 当前节拍 可以已更新。加载列表时会自动进行计算。然后你你已选择的行。
该列表基于组件数据（计划设置）。
计算基础
在这里你可以看到用于计算程序中的订单数量的计算基础的描述。
AV=年度用量
HC=利息
OC=订购费用
组件价值=阅读更多有关组件价值的更多信息 [列表](tList.htm) 章节。

#### 威尔逊公式
OK周=√((2*OC*AV)/(HC*组件价值))

#### 每年订单数量
OKA=每年订单数量/AV

title: 用量价值分析
content:
## 用量价值分析
此程序用于基于价格和年度用量分析具有ABC 代码和用量价值的组件。你还可以在此程序中对组件分类，并更新组件的ABC 代码。分类是根据数量的限制值、总体积值的百分比或组件数量的百分比进行的。

#### ABC 代码
不同体积值的组件使用ABC 代码进行分类。全部使用的ABC 代码都必须在 基本数据表 - 组件 程序。你可以人工的登记为组件的ABC 代码 组件登记 和 组件列表 但此程序中ABC 代码是基于组件的用量价值程序已计算和已建议的。
ABC 代码的目的是用尽可能少的组件捕获尽可能大的用量价值。在开始你运行，你可以调整针对不同分类的已建议限制值。
例如，用于高值组件的ABC 代码的组件应代表用量价值的 80％，另一个ABC 代码的 10％ 代表值稍低的组件，三分之一的ABC 代码代码为 5％，第四部分为 3％，第五部分为 2％。另一种方法是在计算时使用金额限制。例如：用量价值大于100,000 的组件将成为A 组件。用量价值在中间的组件将成为B 组件。
在计算中，程序会努力利用这些份额或用量价值金额限制对组件分类，使其尽可能关闭这些限制值。这是通过按降序用量价值排序对列表进行订单来实现的。然后已计算行的累计值。然后将该累积值以百分比形式用于分类。时间, 该程序基于零件 的当前用量价值, 为组件提供右边 的ABC 代码建议 .
这样，你就可以轻松识别代表用量价值最大的份额或部分的组件。这些组件要么值高，要么年度用量大，或者是两者兼而有之。在系统中的大多数列表中， ABC 代码可用作选择板条款。在基于积极处理组件的重要来区分组件时，它们很有用。
列表类型

#### 显示用量价值
在此列表中，你可以看到组件的用量价值，该值基于其年度用量和价格计算的。此列表否做出新建的分类。

title: 默认值
content:
### 默认值
在此框中你输入已选择模板的阶段 / 活动和成本的默认值。

#### 阶段 / 活动
在此标签页下，你可以在模板中添加默认阶段和活动。第一个，添加阶段你行，然后为该阶段中的活动添加一或多多个子行。一个活动总是属于一个阶段。一个阶段必须总是包含至少一活动。
你可以选择负责人阶段和活动的用户。对于一项活动，你还可以添加评论，链接文件，输入计划时间，等候时间，并选择默认状态。你可以决定是否应在文档上已打印/显示该活动。你还可以创建提醒并决定该活动是否是强制的。你可以标记该活动是否需要收费。
关于计划时间和活动收费的设置可从名为“活动”的主要的标签页中加载。

#### 成本
在此标签页下，你可以在模板中添加默认成本。添加每个行你一。对于每个成本，你可以输入本位币的金额，并标记是否应收取该成本。
关于成本和成本成本的设置可从名为“成本”的主要的标签页中加载。

### 案件类型
标准中包含四种基本类型的相应案件类型。这些基本类型和案件类型是：客户不合格品、供应商不合格品、内部不合格品、和8D 标准。你还可以登记自己的案件类型并将其链接至一基本类型。
你可以输入 前缀 1-3 个字符和一个 优先级 每个案件类型为 1-9。检查 激活的 框中列出了你希望激活的案件类型。

输入 成本 并检查 德 如需收取成本，请填写此框。费用成本意味着该成本将不被用于在案件总成本中。

title: 模板 / 默认
content:
### 模板 / 默认
当你在其它选项卡下已创建数据后，你可以在此标签页下创建模板并为不同案件类型登记默认值。当你稍后登记案件时，用户可以选择使用哪个模板，然后将收到已建议的阶段、活动和成本。
你在表格你标记的模板是一在 默认值 盒子。

#### 案件类型
选择你想要上班的案件类型。你可以为每个案件类型创建一或多个模板。为了 8D 标准 有一个预定义的模板。

#### 默认
你可以在此决定已选择案件类型的新建案件的默认模板。

#### 名称
你可以在此处写一段描述性文本作为名称。你使用公司语言输入名称文本，并以用户的语言显示。

#### 翻译
使用按钮 翻译 ![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/button_translate.png)s 你可以将文本翻译为系统中已登记的不同激活语言。阅读更多内容 [语言管理](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/GeneralFeatures.htm#LanguageManagement) 用于可翻译文本。

title: 基本数据表 - 案件
content:
## 基本数据表 - 案件
在此程序中，你需要在你第一个案件或不合格情况之前登记基础数据。你登记案件类型、成本、阶段，并每案件类型配置默认值。对于 8D方式，还有一个预定义的模板作为质量工作的支持。

title: 详细 - 案件列表
content:
### 详细 - 案件列表
此列表类型按详细视图中的按案件分组。每个案件都显示在列表中的单独行上。一些列已经合并。这些列显示客户号或供应商号，以及客户名称或供应商名称。由于一个案件不能两者填写客户和供应商的信息，列采用了这种设计。这也适用于案件号和联系人。

#### 拒收数量
在此列，你可以看到该案件拒收数量。

#### 已计划和实际成本
在这些列，你可以看到案件全部成本的合计。这可以每基本类型显示，例如，全部客户偏差都总计起来。这也可以显示为每客户的合计。你将在列表底部看到整个列表的合计。

title: 详细 - 成本列表
content:
### 详细 - 成本列表
此列表类型按详细视图中的按案件分组。案件i 的成本按不同成本类型划分。有一列为计划成本，一列为实际成本。

title: 详细 - 客户 / 供应商列表
heading_path: 详细 - 客户 / 供应商列表
content:
### 详细 - 客户 / 供应商列表
此列表类型按详细视图中的按客户 / 供应商分组。每个客户 / 供应商都显示在列表中的单独行上。一些列已经合并。这些列显示客户号或供应商号，以及客户名称或供应商名称。由于一个案件不能两者填写客户和供应商的信息，列采用了这种设计。

#### 拒收数量
在此列，你可以看到相关客户 / 供应商的拒收数量。

#### 已计划和实际成本

title: 详细 - 组件列表

title: 按案件分组组件列表类型分组的部分

content:

title: 合计 - 客户 / 供应商列表

content:

content:

title: 案件列表
content:
## 案件列表
在此程序中，你可以在不同的列表中显示案件。你可以载入打开案件两者已关闭/历史案件。你创建的列表基于已登记的案件及其相关信息（自客户、供应商、组件等加载）。不更新这些列表中的信息。
> 拒收代码和拒收数量主要为已输入的案件已确认信息。如果案件不输入此项，则将应用基本信息中输入的拒收数量和拒收代码。
列表类型

此列表类型是按客户 / 供应商合计的。每个客户 / 供应商都显示在列表中的单独行上。每个客户号/供应商号前面都有一个用于钻取功能的按钮。使用它你可以视图属于客户 / 供应商的案件的详细信息。

#### 合计 - 组件
此列表类型为按组件合计。每个组件都显示在列表中单独的行上。每个组件号前面都有一个用于钻取功能的按钮。使用它你可以视图属于该组件的案件的详细信息。

#### 详细 - 案件
此列表类型按详细视图中的按案件分组。每个案件都显示在列表中的单独行上。一些列已经合并。这些列显示客户号或供应商号，以及客户名称或供应商名称。由于一个案件不能两者填写客户和供应商的信息，列采用了这种设计。这也适用于案件号和联系人。

#### 详细 - 客户 / 供应商
此列表类型按客户分组/供应商分组显示详细视图。每个客户 / 供应商都显示在列表中的单独行上。一些列已经合并。这些列显示客户案件号或供应商案件号，以及客户联系人或供应商联系人。由于一个案件不能两者填写客户和供应商的信息，列采用了这种设计。

#### 详细 - 组件
此列表类型按详细视图中的按组件分组。每个组件都显示在列表中单独的行上。一些列已经合并。这些列显示客户号或供应商号，以及客户名称或供应商名称。由于一个案件不能两者填写客户和供应商的信息，列采用了这种设计。这也适用于案件号和联系人。

#### 详细 - 成本
此列表类型按详细视图中的按案件分组。案件i 的成本按不同成本类型划分。有一列为实际成本，一列为计划成本。

title: 案件列表
content:
#### 按案件分组组件
此列表类型按案件分组显示详细视图，并显示每个案件被用于哪些组件。该列表还显示案件中哪个组件是默认的（主组件/第一个组件），以及组件的​​序列号/批次号。
格式
演示文稿确定了如何显示/呈现所选列表。例如，应将其作为分组显示还是作为总计显示。该程序中包含一些标准格式。
在大多数可以加载列表的程序中，可以创建自己的格式。这是在相关程序后台的格式下完成的。例如，如果您创建自己的格式，您可选择它是否应该具有钻取功能和钻取过滤器。
您可选择列表应包含哪些列，并且可以为每一列配置分组、排序、聚合，以及该列是否应以图表形式显示以及是否应打印。此外，您还可以进行打印输出设置、图表设置和有关额外聚合的设置。
在[格式](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/Presentations.htm)中阅读有关此内容的更多信息。
选择列
在列表程序中，始终有一个名为选择的标签页，您可以在其中选择数据库中不同间隔的数据记录。然后使用程序工具栏中的载入按钮![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/button_display_list.png)加载数据记录。
在程序后台的选择行下，您可调整位于选择标签页每种列表类型应具有的选择行。在列表类型字段中，您可选择要自定义选择行的列表类型。
一张表显示可以选择的选择行，一张表显示已选定的选择行。您可通过使用鼠标指针拖放来添加、删除或移动选择行。
使用保存按钮![](https://help.monitorerp.cn/CN-MONITOR_G5/zh-cn/Content/Resources/Images/button_save.png)保存选定的选择行。
在[选择](../../../UserGuide/GeneralFeatures/Selection.htm)主题中阅读有关此内容的更多信息。
